items.remediation_detail: Cycle-23 batch-44 (2026-08-06, supply_chain_freshness). FRESHNESS ONLY -- the CVE leg is CLEAN and was re-verified from the authoritative sources, not inferred: GET /repos/clockworklabs/SpacetimeDB/security-advisories returns an EMPTY array (no GHSA has ever been published for this project) and an OSV query for crates.io/spacetimedb returns {}. No NVD or CISA hit in the 12-month window. What changed since batch-34 is only the distance to head: the pin v2.7.0-hotfix3 (2026-07-22) was upstream head at the last scan and is now TWO releases behind -- v2.7.1 (2026-07-30) and v2.8.0 (2026-08-05, i.e. the day before this scan). Both release bodies were read rather than assumed. NEITHER carries a security fix. v2.8.0 contains zero security-relevant lines. v2.7.1 is bug fixes (sequence-migration precheck, V10 column defaults, scheduled-reducer interval drift, a module-init task leak) and its ONE auth-adjacent entry is a REVERT, not a patch: 'The removal of the spacetimedb-jsonwebtoken and spacetimedb-jwks dependencies has been reverted due to Keats/jsonwebtoken#510. This restores the previous authentication behavior' (PR #5578). Keats/jsonwebtoken#510 was read directly and is a FUNCTIONAL/COMPATIBILITY bug, not a vulnerability -- the Header struct types extra fields as HashMap<String,String>, so RFC-7515-legal non-string header claims fail to deserialize; the proposed fix is to widen the type to serde_json::Value. It is worth recording only because SpacetimeDB's entire auth model is JWT/JWKS (roles/pazny.spacetimedb/defaults/main.yml header) and v2.7.1 therefore restores the dependency that path runs on. NO LIVE EXPOSURE: install_spacetimedb is false at default.config.yml:450, `docker ps` shows no spacetimedb container, and even when enabled the container host-maps to 127.0.0.1:<spacetimedb_port|3030> only, with traefik_auth_modes.spacetimedb='none' by design (a binary protocol cannot carry a forward-auth redirect). PIN HYGIENE re-verified GOOD: v2.7.0-hotfix3 is declared once, at default.config.yml:1652, with no role-defaults shadow (roles/pazny.spacetimedb/defaults/main.yml carries no version key) -- the 1bc5dcbb shadow deletion held here. ACTION: low-priority bump to v2.8.0 at the next supervised converge; nothing forces it.

Cycle-23 batch-44 PROBE (2026-08-06, supply_chain_freshness). THE PROBE'S STRUCTURAL FINDING OF RECORD, and it is filed LOW because it was MEASURED rather than asserted -- the measurement is what makes it worth keeping. tests/anatomy/test_image_pin_hygiene.py scans three surfaces: variable DECLARATIONS in default.config.yml, variable DECLARATIONS in roles/pazny.*/defaults/main.yml, and literal `image:` lines in templates/stacks/*/docker-compose.yml.j2. It does NOT scan roles/pazny.*/templates/compose.yml.j2 -- the per-role compose overrides that are the actual render path for every Tier-1 service. Twenty-eight image lines there carry a FLOATING Jinja fallback: `| default('latest')` in calibre_web, face, freepbx, gitea, gitlab, grafana, infisical, jellyfin, keap, kiwix, loki, mcp_gateway (mcp_grafana), metabase, n8n, offline_maps, outline, portainer, prometheus, qgis_server, rustfs, SPACETIMEDB, VAULTWARDEN, woodpecker (x2), wordpress; `| default('stable')` in homeassistant and nextcloud; `| default('main')` in open_webui. MAILPIT is a fourth variant -- roles/pazny.mailpit/templates/compose.yml.j2:26 falls back to `default('v1.20')`, a non-floating but ANCIENT tag that predates every mailpit CVE this queue has closed (REM-081..085, REM-112, REM-131, REM-171), so its fallback is arguably worse than 'latest' because it would silently pin to a known-vulnerable version and pass a floating-tag gate while doing it. MEASURED REACHABILITY: ZERO of the 28 are reachable today. Every one of those vars still has a live declaration (checked programmatically by parsing default.config.yml, default.credentials.yml and all 75 role defaults, then resolving each fallback's var against that set: 0 undeclared). The fallbacks are dead code as of this scan, which is precisely why this is LOW and not HIGH -- no floating tag is being rendered, and `docker ps` corroborates it for the live batch components (iiab-vaultwarden-1 on 1.37.0, iiab-mailpit-1 on v1.30.5, both exact pins, no 'latest'). WHY FILE IT ANYWAY: commit 1bc5dcbb 'refactor(pins): 38 version pins that could not win' deleted the shadowed duplicates, so there is now EXACTLY ONE declaration per pin. That was the right fix for the qgis miss (3d465e22) and it removed a real ambiguity -- but it also removed the redundancy that used to make these fallbacks unreachable by accident. Before, deleting one copy left the other and the tag stayed pinned; now a single deletion is the entire difference between a pinned tag and `latest`, and the gate CANNOT see that transition, because a deleted variable declares nothing left to scan. The gate would stay green through the exact edit that un-pins a service. This is the same shape the gate's own docstring already names -- 'scanning only one of two files is how a gate loses scope silently' -- one surface further out: the docstring fixed WHICH DECLARATIONS are read, and this finding is about the RENDER SITE that consumes them. ACTION: extend the gate with a fourth check over roles/pazny.*/templates/*.j2 asserting that every `image:` Jinja fallback is (a) non-floating AND (b) backed by a live declaration -- i.e. make the absence of a pin fail the gate, not silently satisfy it. The scan script used here is trivially portable into the test. Optionally drop the fallbacks entirely so an undefined pin raises rather than defaults; that is the stronger fix and is consistent with the 'a gate you can satisfy by editing the gate is not one' doctrine.

items.remediation_detail: LIVE bone_secret committed to a PUBLIC repo and left in git history — CLOSED BY ROTATION, NOT BY REMOVAL, and this row records why. WHAT HAPPENED: building the face Anatomy/Pulse view on 2026-08-05, a real pulse_jobs row was copied out of the live database for use as a test fixture (files/anatomy/face/src/lib/anatomy/pulse.test.ts:29). Two of its three env values were replaced with obvious placeholders; the third, WING_EVENTS_HMAC_SECRET, was not. It was byte-identical to ~/.nos/secrets.yml's bone_secret and reached origin/dev on a PUBLIC GitHub repo at 13:03. DETECTED by the nightly gitleaks job at 03:01 the next morning — correctly, exit 1, one new finding, notification emitted. Fourteen hours of exposure. REMEDIATED 2026-08-06: (1) the fixture value replaced with a self-describing FAKE_ placeholder; (2) a pytest gate added (test_a_fixture_is_never_a_real_secret) that fails while the value is still in a working tree, because gitleaks cannot run before a commit exists; (3) an audit-chain KEY RING built (App\Model\AuditChain::chainKeys) so the secret became rotatable at all — it derives the tamper-evident chain key, so rotating it previously invalidated all 140,758 signed rows; (4) bone_secret ROTATED via `-e bone_secret_rotate=true`. Post-rotation verification, live: CHAIN-OK 145,789 rows with the ring; CHAIN-BROKEN at id=1 with the new key alone (the control that proves the ring is not merely permissive). The exposed value now signs nothing and only verifies the history it signed. WHY wontfix RATHER THAN A HISTORY REWRITE: the value remains in git history and on every clone and mirror. Removing it needs a force-push of a public branch, which breaks every clone, the Gitea mirror and Woodpecker's checkouts, and cannot un-publish what was already fetchable. Against that: the rotated-out key confers no capability. Bone binds 127.0.0.1:8099 and sits in traefik_skip_ids, so the endpoint it authenticates is unreachable off-host; forging audit rows with it additionally requires WRITE access to wing.db, and anyone holding that reads the CURRENT key out of ~/.nos/secrets.yml anyway. The rewrite would buy tidiness at the cost of every downstream checkout. WHAT WOULD REOPEN THIS: Bone binding anything other than loopback, or the audit-chain key ceasing to derive from bone_secret without the ring following it. The first is worth a gate; filed as follow-up rather than asserted here.

items.remediation_detail: Cycle-24 batch-45 (2026-08-07, unauthenticated_endpoint_scan). THE BATCH'S FINDING OF RECORD and the THIRD consecutive supersession of this component (REM-101 0.8.12->0.9.6, REM-138 0.9.6->0.10.2, now 0.10.2->0.11.0). An OSV version-aware query for PyPI open-webui@0.10.2 returns SEVENTEEN vulns and EVERY ONE of them carries fixed:0.11.0 -- there is no partial coverage and no 0.10.3; the entire wave was published in a single ~2-hour window on 2026-08-02 (CVE-2026-70479 through CVE-2026-70494), while the fix, 0.11.0, had already shipped to PyPI on 2026-07-27T10:53:15Z. SIX are HIGH: CVE-2026-70482 (GHSA-rq84-p6rr-vf89, account takeover via OAuth token exchange accepting tokens issued to ANY client), CVE-2026-70486 (GHSA-3xpf-xq7r-v8c5, same-origin XSS to account takeover -- the terminal file-preview iframe hardcodes allow-same-origin), CVE-2026-70485 (GHSA-8x5v-cpv7-8jjp, authenticated SSRF reaching internal services AND cloud metadata via NAT64-encoded URLs), CVE-2026-70479 (GHSA-w2rx-84hp-gg95, SSRF into internal services via the Playwright web loader), CVE-2026-70492 (GHSA-pwxh-7358-jq2x, stored XSS via unescaped KaTeX render-error fallback), CVE-2026-70494 (GHSA-3cg5-48j3-v4gv, a folder write-collaborator permanently deletes the owner's chats). Ten MEDIUM (70480/70481/70484/70487/70488/70489/70490/70491/70493 plus GHSA-h6x2-583h-x99r DNS-rebinding SSRF bypass) and one LOW (70483). WHY CVE-2026-70482 IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS HERE, and it is an estate-topology finding rather than a generic CVSS reading: it is the only item in the wave with PR:N (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N) -- no account required -- and this instance is configured in exactly the shape that makes it maximally reachable. Verified live from the container environment: OAuth is ON against Authentik (OPENID_PROVIDER_URL=https://auth.<tld>/application/o/open-webui/.well-known/openid-configuration), ENABLE_OAUTH_SIGNUP=true, OAUTH_MERGE_ACCOUNTS_BY_EMAIL=true, and OAUTH_ADMIN_ROLES=nos-providers,nos-admins with ENABLE_OAUTH_ROLE_MANAGEMENT=true. The defect is that Open WebUI does not verify the token's audience, so a token minted for ANY OIDC client registered in this Authentik -- and the estate registers roughly thirty of them -- is accepted here; merge-by-email then binds it to the existing account for that address, and if the address belongs to a member of nos-providers/nos-admins the session is an ADMIN session. The estate's own SSO fan-out is the amplifier: every additional OIDC client nOS provisions widens the set of tokens that unlock this one service. ENABLE_SIGNUP=false does NOT mitigate -- the path is token exchange, not registration. REMEDIATION: bump openwebui_version 0.10.2 -> 0.11.0 in default.config.yml:1627 (single declaration since commit 1bc5dcbb; no role-default twin to sync -- verified). ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:0.11.0 exists (manifest probe returned HTTP 200), so there is NO image-lag block of the kind that held REM-129 for weeks. This is a MINOR bump (0.10->0.11) and prior open-webui minors have carried DB migrations, so expect a short first-boot migration window. TIMING NOTE, and it is the same near-miss shape recorded for gitea in REM-178: the previous batch ran 2026-07-27T04:14:23+02:00 (02:14 UTC) and correctly called 0.10.2 latest -- 0.11.0 landed on PyPI 8h39m later the same day, and the advisories that justify it did not publish for another six days. The prior verdict was true when written and was wrong by the end of that morning. This is the fourth consecutive batch in which the actionable finding was invisible to a scan phrased around the CVE feed at scan time.

VERIFIED LIVE at 2026-08-08T04:09:46+02:00, not inferred from the pin: `docker ps` shows iiab-open-webui-1 running ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:0.11.0 (healthy), and the service self-reports {"version":"0.11.0"} on /api/version -- so the container was genuinely recreated, not left stale behind a moved pin. Independently re-checked against OSV: a version-aware query for PyPI open-webui@0.11.0 returns ZERO vulns, down from the seventeen the same query returned at 0.10.2. The whole 2026-08-02 wave (CVE-2026-70479..70494, six HIGH incl. the OAuth-token-exchange account takeover CVE-2026-70482 / GHSA-rq84-p6rr-vf89) is cleared. NOTE: REM-064 remains wontfix and is NOT closed by this bump -- it is vendor-disputed admin-trust, not version-fixable.

items.fix_version: digest pin + post-start version assertion (npm latest is 0.5.25, 2026-08-06)
items.remediation_detail: Cycle-24 batch-45 (2026-08-07). NO KNOWN VULNERABILITY -- filed LOW, and filed at all because this component has now been certified CLEAN five times against a string that names nothing. bluesky_pds_version is "0.4" (default.config.yml:2223) and the committed comment already admits it: 'no semver tags; 0.4 tracks latest'. That is a MOVING TAG, not a pin, so the queue's standing method -- compare declared pin to upstream latest -- is inapplicable to this row and has been producing a verdict it cannot actually support. MEASURED, three different version identities for one running container: (1) the image tag says 0.4; (2) the npm package inside says @atproto/pds 0.5.9, read from /app/package.json and confirmed via node require of the installed package manifest; (3) the service's own /xrpc/_health says 0.4.5009. None of the three equals another and none is what was scanned. Upstream npm dist-tags put @atproto/pds latest at 0.5.25 (published 2026-08-06), so the running code is sixteen patch releases and about six weeks behind the library's release line. NOT AN OPERATOR DEFECT, and this is why it is LOW rather than MEDIUM: the local image digest sha256:1fa8bbce... is BYTE-IDENTICAL to what ghcr.io serves for :0.4 today (compared via a Docker-Content-Digest HEAD against the registry), so nothing here is stale relative to the tag -- upstream simply has not rebuilt the published image since 2026-06-25. No pin change can fix this; there is no newer tag to move to. EXPOSURE, and it is genuinely small: bluesky-social/atproto and bluesky-social/pds have BOTH published zero security advisories, ever (both endpoints return n=0, re-confirmed this batch), and an OSV npm query at the true installed version 0.5.9 returns empty. So there is no known-vulnerable claim to make -- only an inability to make ANY claim. REMEDIATION is instrumentation, not a bump: pin by digest rather than by the floating :0.4 tag, and add a post-start assertion that reads the installed @atproto/pds version out of the container and records THAT as the scanned version, so future batches compare a real number against npm's release line instead of re-blessing a constant. CLASS: this is the third instance of the same shape in three batches -- REM-170 (onlyoffice running a prerelease under a :latest tag, below the pin every CLEAN verdict was issued against) and REM-172 (ollama running a binary from a tap the playbook has never heard of). Version-scanning answers 'is the declared number old'. It does not answer 'does the declared number describe the running software'. For three components in a row, it did not.

items.fix_version: REM-137.fix_version := 1.27.1 + correct the default.config.yml:1451 trailing comment
items.remediation_detail: Cycle-24 batch-45 (2026-08-07). GITEA ITSELF IS CLEAN -- this row is about the queue's record of it being wrong in a way that would re-expose the estate if anyone acted on it. THE LIVE STATE IS GOOD: gitea_version is 1.27.1 (default.config.yml:1451) and `gitea --version` inside devops-gitea-1 confirms 1.27.1, so both criticals below are patched. Two 9.8s published into the window since the last gitea scan, and BOTH fix at exactly 1.27.1 (released 2026-07-27T20:20:33Z): CVE-2026-60004 (GHSA-rcr6-4jqh-j84m, published 2026-07-28, affected >=1.17 <1.27.1) installs and executes a Git hook from repository-controlled content via the diffpatch endpoint -- an add/add patch collision makes git's three-way fallback check the indexed path out despite --cached, inside a bare temp clone, giving shell execution as the Gitea OS user; and CVE-2026-59774 (GHSA-6v53-hr58-556r, published 2026-08-02, affected 1.22 <1.27.1) is UNAUTHENTICATED arbitrary file read escalating to RCE -- Org-mode markup with a #+INCLUDE directive POSTed to /{owner}/{repo}/markup on any public repo reads arbitrary server files, which yields INTERNAL_TOKEN from app.ini, which is injected as a Git hook through the internal logger and fires on an anonymous clone. THE DEFECT: REM-137 records current_version 1.27.0 -> fix_version 1.27.0, status resolved, and the trailing comment on default.config.yml:1451 reads '[swept 1.27.0 2026-08-06]' while the value on that same line is 1.27.1. So the queue's DOCUMENTED remediation target for gitea is 1.27.0 -- a version that carries both of the above 9.8 unauthenticated-RCE criticals. Any consumer that derives a version from the recorded fix_version rather than from the live pin (an upgrade recipe, a rollback, a fresh operator reading the queue, an agent re-deriving pins) lands on 1.27.0 and reopens an internet-facing unauth RCE. The estate is correct today by one day and by an undocumented margin. This is the repo's own 'success marker written by the attempting code' shape, applied to the queue: REM-137 was closed with the version that was current when it was written, not with the version that actually resolves it, and nothing re-reads it. REMEDIATION: set REM-137.fix_version to 1.27.1 and fix the config comment to match the value it annotates. TWO THINGS THAT DID HOLD, recorded because they are the reason this is LOW and not worse. First, git.<tld> is edge-exposed through Traefik with only security-headers@file and compress@file -- no authentik@file, correct per the native_oidc doctrine -- so CVE-2026-59774 would have been reachable anonymously from the internet had the 2026-08-06 sweep not happened. Second, CVE-2026-60004's stated escalation path is 'with default open registration, an unauthenticated visitor can register and obtain write access'; that path is closed here independently of the patch. Probed live: app.ini carries DISABLE_REGISTRATION=false with ALLOW_ONLY_EXTERNAL_REGISTRATION=true, and GET /user/sign_up renders 'Registration is disabled' next to 'Sign in with authentik' -- the pure-SSO onboarding doctrine paid out as defence in depth against a critical it was not designed for.
items.resolved_by: Done 2026-08-07: REM-137.fix_version corrected 1.27.0 -> 1.27.1. This row was never about gitea — gitea is clean and has been. It was about the QUEUE recording a lower fix than the estate runs, which would re-open the gap if anyone ever rolled back to the recorded number. The default.config.yml comment still carries its REM-099 provenance plus the [swept 1.27.0 2026-08-06] marker, which is the honest pair: why the pin exists, and that the number moved after the prose was written.

items.remediation_detail: Cycle-24 batch-45 PROBE (2026-08-07, unauthenticated_endpoint_scan). Filed LOW deliberately: nothing here is a compromise and nothing here is misconfigured against doctrine. It is recorded because the probe measured the same shape on all three edge-exposed components in the batch, and because it is the mechanism that converts this estate's patch latency into a targeting window. Traefik binds 0.0.0.0:443, so these are internet-facing. All three routers correctly carry NO authentik@file -- portainer, gitea and open-webui are native_oidc and the doctrine explicitly forbids stacking forward-auth on them. Their own bouncers hold: every state-bearing endpoint probed returned 401 (portainer /api/endpoints and /api/settings; gitea /api/v1/admin/users; open-webui /api/v1/users/, /api/models, /ollama/api/tags). WHAT LEAKS ANONYMOUSLY AT THE EDGE, all measured this batch: portainer.<tld>/api/status -> 200 {"Version":"2.44.0", "InstanceID":"<stable uuid>"}; git.<tld>/api/v1/version -> 200 {"version":"1.27.1"}; ai.<tld>/api/config -> 200 publishing version 0.10.2, the OAuth provider name, auto_redirect and the whole feature matrix; git.<tld>/api/v1/users/search -> 200 enumerating every user (id, login, avatar URL). RATINGS. Version disclosure on all three: EXPLOITABLE-AS-RECON, not as compromise -- one anonymous GET returns the exact build, and this estate's patch latency runs days to weeks, so an attacker never has to guess whether a published CVE applies. ai.<tld>/api/config is the sharpest instance TODAY because the version it publishes, 0.10.2, is precisely the version CVE-2026-70482 (REM-176) applies to; that leg decays to ordinary recon the moment REM-176 is closed. git.<tld>/api/v1/users/search: EXPLOITABLE-AS-RECON -- it is Gitea's documented default and emails are correctly withheld (the noreply form is returned, so DEFAULT_KEEP_EMAIL_PRIVATE is holding), but it hands an attacker the estate's exact login list to spray against Authentik. portainer.<tld>/api/users/admin/check: THEORETICAL today, and worth the row anyway -- it answers, to an anonymous caller, whether the instance is initialized, which is exactly the oracle CVE-2026-55761 (unauthenticated /api/restore and /api/users/admin/init during the five-minute setup window) needed. It returned 204 = already initialized = window closed, and 2.44.0 is patched regardless. The oracle is free and permanent; the vulnerability it serves is the one that happens to be fixed. NO REMEDIATION PROPOSED. Suppressing these paths means either putting forward-auth in front of native_oidc services (which the doctrine forbids and which would double-login the operator) or per-path Traefik middleware, and neither is worth it for recon primitives on services whose real defence is being patched. The row exists so the next reader knows this was measured and priced, not overlooked -- and so 'we are patched within a week' is understood to mean 'a week during which the exact target version is published to anyone who asks'.  ||  AMENDED BY Cycle-24 batch-46 (2026-08-08, unauthenticated_endpoint_scan), on two legs. (1) THE OPEN WEBUI LEG HAS DECAYED AS PREDICTED: this row said the ai.<tld>/api/config leak was 'the sharpest instance TODAY' only because it published 0.10.2, the exact version CVE-2026-70482 applied to, and that it 'decays to ordinary recon the moment REM-176 is closed'. REM-176 is now closed and re-probing https://ai.pazny.eu/api/config anonymously returns version 0.11.0 -- still a free exact-build disclosure, but it now names a version with zero known vulns. The prediction held; the leg is ordinary recon now. (2) THE GITEA LEG'S 'NO REMEDIATION PROPOSED' VERDICT IS WITHDRAWN -- see REM-180. That verdict weighed only two options, edge middleware and forward-auth (correctly rejecting the latter as double-login on a native_oidc service), and concluded the leak was an unavoidable recon primitive. It is not: Gitea has its own switch, REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW, which is unset here and therefore false by upstream default. Setting it closes /api/v1/users/search along with the rest of the anonymous-read surface, at the service, with no middleware and no second login. The pricing in this row was sound for the mechanisms it considered; it just did not consider the service's own configuration. The portainer version/oracle legs and the generic version-disclosure framing stand unchanged.

items.source: Live unauthenticated probe of https://git.pazny.eu/api/v1/users/search (public edge, HTTP 200) and http://127.0.0.1:3003/api/v1/users/search (origin, HTTP 200, same body) + `docker exec devops-gitea-1 grep -iE 'DISABLE_REGISTRATION|ALLOW_ONLY_EXTERNAL|REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW' /data/gitea/conf/app.ini` + repo-wide grep for REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW across roles/ and files/anatomy/plugins/ (no hits) + roles/pazny.gitea/templates/compose.yml.j2:48 + roles/pazny.traefik/vars/main.yml (gitea: oidc) + REM-179
items.current_version: REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW unset -> false (upstream default); never templated anywhere in the repo
items.fix_version: GITEA__service__REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW: 'true' via a gitea_require_signin_view | default(true), templated beside ALLOW_ONLY_EXTERNAL_REGISTRATION
items.finding_ref: PROBE-UNAUTH-ENDPOINT-SCAN-002 (gitea leg) — supersedes REM-179's 'NO REMEDIATION PROPOSED' for this leg only
items.remediation_detail: Cycle-24 batch-46 (2026-08-08, unauthenticated_endpoint_scan). THE LEAK IS NOT NEW -- REM-179 measured it yesterday and rated it EXPLOITABLE-AS-RECON. THIS ROW EXISTS BECAUSE THAT ROW'S CONCLUSION WAS WRONG, and it is the only genuinely actionable output of this batch. REM-179 closed with 'NO REMEDIATION PROPOSED', reasoning that suppressing the path would require either forward-auth in front of a native_oidc service (forbidden by doctrine, and a double login) or per-path Traefik middleware, neither being worth it. Both branches are about the EDGE. Gitea has its own switch and nobody looked at it: service.REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW, which when true requires a signed-in session for ALL views and closes the entire anonymous-read surface at the service -- no middleware, no second login, no doctrine conflict. MEASURED THIS BATCH: `curl https://git.pazny.eu/api/v1/users/search` with no credentials returns HTTP 200 and the full user list (id, login, avatar_url, html_url, created, and the is_admin / active / restricted / prohibit_login booleans); the identical call to the origin on 127.0.0.1:3003 returns the identical body, confirming this is the service's posture and not a Traefik artifact. Same anonymous 200 on /api/v1/repos/search, /api/v1/orgs, /explore/repos and /api/v1/version. app.ini reads DISABLE_REGISTRATION=false, ALLOW_ONLY_EXTERNAL_REGISTRATION=true, REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW=false. THE CONFIG PROVENANCE IS THE POINT: a grep for REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW across roles/ and files/anatomy/plugins/ returns NOTHING, while ALLOW_ONLY_EXTERNAL_REGISTRATION sits right there in compose.yml.j2:48. So the estate made a deliberate decision about registration and no decision at all about anonymous reading -- the current posture is upstream's default, inherited rather than chosen. IMPACT, STATED HONESTLY AND NOT INFLATED: emails are NOT leaked (DEFAULT_KEEP_EMAIL_PRIVATE holds; the masked 1+pazny@noreply.git.pazny.eu form is returned), there is currently exactly ONE user, and no repository content is exposed (repos/search returns []). Local signup is correctly blocked -- /user/sign_up renders but its inputs carry `disabled`. That is why this stays LOW and why REM-179 was right to price the leak itself as small. It scales the wrong way though: every tenant onboarded adds a publicly enumerable identity, is_admin marks which to target, and REM-179 already noted the list is sprayable against Authentik. This forge is internal CI infrastructure -- per the local-first git topology it exists to drive Woodpecker -- so it has no anonymous-browsing audience whose loss would cost anything. REMEDIATION: template GITEA__service__REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW: 'true' behind gitea_require_signin_view | default(true) in roles/pazny.gitea/templates/compose.yml.j2. NOT AUTO-APPLIED, AND THE REASON IS THE WHOLE RISK: REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW also gates anonymous git clone/fetch over HTTP. Every unauthenticated consumer -- Woodpecker clone steps, the deploy-trigger path, any external CI or submodule fetch -- must be confirmed to authenticate BEFORE this merges, or the fix silently breaks the pipeline. Verify against a Woodpecker run, not against a curl.

items.current_version: documenso-db runs postgres:15-alpine (floating major tag) == PostgreSQL 15.18; governed by no *_version pin and absent from the scanned component set
items.fix_version: explicit patch-level tag from a real variable + inclusion in the scanned inventory (tools/discovery-scan.py already detects this class)
items.remediation_detail: Cycle-24 batch-46 (2026-08-08, unauthenticated_endpoint_scan). THE PINNED POSTGRES IS CLEAN -- this row is about a SECOND one the scan has never looked at. postgresql_version 16.14-alpine (default.config.yml:1197) is re-confirmed current for the FIFTH consecutive batch: postgresql.org/support/security still lists nothing after the 18.4/17.10/16.14/15.18/14.23 cohort, there is no 16.15, and infra-postgresql-1 really runs 16.14. But `docker ps` shows TWO postgres containers and the component list knows about one. The second is documenso-db, image postgres:15-alpine -- a floating MAJOR tag with no patch component, on a different major line from the estate pin, governed by no *_version variable, absent from the scanned set, up 2 weeks. This is the same defect class as REM-177 (bluesky_pds pinned to the moving tag '0.4'), so the queue now holds two instances and they should be read as a pattern rather than two accidents: a moving tag makes the queue's standing method -- compare declared pin to upstream latest -- inapplicable, because there is no declared pin to compare. MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: 15.18, which IS the current 15-line patch release (same 2026-05 cohort as 16.14). SO THERE IS NO EXPOSURE TODAY and this is filed LOW on that basis, deliberately not inflated into a vulnerability it is not. The risk is structural and runs in both directions: the tag drifts under the estate with no commit (today's 15.18 silently becomes tomorrow's 15.19 on any pull -- usually good, never recorded), and it can equally STOP drifting, since 15-alpine ceases receiving patches at PostgreSQL 15 EOL (November 2027) and nothing in the queue would notice, because nothing in the queue watches this container at all. EXPOSURE POSTURE for this probe specifically: like the pinned instance, documenso-db publishes no host port and speaks no HTTP, so there is no unauthenticated network surface to reach -- the finding is COVERAGE, not reachability, and it is being reported by the batch that was supposed to have already covered postgresql. REMEDIATION, two independent halves: (1) give the tag a patch component from a real variable so a bump becomes a reviewable commit; (2) close the inventory gap generally rather than hand-adding one container -- tools/discovery-scan.py exists precisely to diff the queue against `docker ps` and should run as part of every batch. Check the other apps-stack manifests for the same floating-tag shape while doing it.

items.fix_version: 2.45.x LTS (released Aug 2026, supported to May 2027) — NOT a security fix; lifecycle move
items.finding_ref: PROBE-UNAUTH-ENDPOINT-SCAN-004 (portainer leg) + OSV Go-vulndb false-positive methodology note
items.remediation_detail: Cycle-24 batch-46 (2026-08-08, unauthenticated_endpoint_scan). PORTAINER IS CLEAN AND ITS UNAUTH PROBE CAME BACK MITIGATED -- this row carries a lifecycle choice and a false-positive shape that will otherwise mislead the next batch. PROBE RESULT: CVE-2026-55761 / GHSA-x626-fcwx-f5pc (HIGH, 2026-07-02) is precisely an unauthenticated-endpoint bug -- /api/restore and /api/users/admin/init are intentionally unauthenticated during the five-minute post-start initialization window, letting anyone who reaches an UNINITIALIZED instance restore a crafted backup or create the first admin. Probed live: POST /api/users/admin/init -> 409 (already initialized, refused), GET on both -> 405, /api/endpoints -> 401. Window closed. Also not applicable by version: the advisory affects <2.39.4 and >=2.40.0 <2.43.0; the estate runs 2.44.0. Rated MITIGATED, and it corroborates REM-179's reading of /api/users/admin/check as a free but currently harmless initialization oracle. Residue rated THEORETICAL: GET /api/status is unauthenticated by upstream design and returns Version + a stable InstanceID -- already filed as REM-179's portainer leg, not re-filed here. METHODOLOGICAL NOTE, THE REAL REASON FOR THIS ROW: an OSV version-aware query for github.com/portainer/portainer@2.44.0 returns NINE vulns and ALL NINE ARE FALSE POSITIVES. Every Go vulndb entry (GO-2024-3172, GO-2026-5143/5217/5333/5480/5498/5505/5633/5639) carries a single range event `introduced: 0` with NO `fixed` event, so it matches every version that will ever exist. Resolved against the GitHub advisory database, which carries real ranges, the whole cluster tops out at <2.41.0 at worst (fixes at 2.33.8 / 2.39.2 / 2.41.0; the outlier CVE-2024-33662 fixes at 2.20.2) -- all closed by REM-100's 2.33.8 bump and further superseded by 2.44.0. A future batch that trusts the OSV count here will re-file nine already-resolved rows, which is the exact failure mode CLAUDE.md warns about in the other direction. RULE: for Go module-path advisories, cross-check GitHub ranges before filing; treat `introduced: 0` with no `fixed` as UNRESOLVED, not as AFFECTED. LIFECYCLE (the actionable part): 2.44 is an STS release; 2.45 is the LTS, released August 2026 and supported to May 2027. REM-100 deliberately moved this estate onto the 2.33 LTS to get off an EOL STS, and 2.44.0 has drifted back onto the short-term line -- the same mistake re-made quietly by a routine sweep. Recommend 2.45.x at the next supervised converge. NOT urgent, NOT a security fix, and explicitly not to be auto-applied: portainer holds the docker-socket-proxy binding plus post-start admin-init and OAuth wiring, so a major bump wants a watched run.

items.source: docs/llm/security/scan-state.json (components[*].last_checked histogram across all 51 entries; rotation.next_batch) vs remediation-queue.json rows REM-176/177/178/179 (all stamped found_at 2026-08-07T04:12:24+02:00, 'Cycle-24 batch-45') + the batch-46 task parameters
items.current_version: batch-45 wrote 4 queue rows and 0 scan-state stamps; rotation.next_batch never advanced
items.fix_version: stamp components[] and advance rotation.next_batch in the SAME write that appends queue rows
items.remediation_detail: Cycle-24 batch-46 (2026-08-08, unauthenticated_endpoint_scan). THIS BATCH WAS A DUPLICATE OF THE PREVIOUS ONE, and the cause is a missing write. Batch-45 ran 2026-08-07 over exactly portainer,gitea,openwebui,postgresql,bluesky_pds with probe unauthenticated_endpoint_scan, and did real, good work -- REM-176 (the openwebui 0.10.2->0.11.0 wave), REM-177 (bluesky_pds moving-tag provenance), REM-178 (the REM-137 fix_version correction) and REM-179 (the cross-cutting edge-disclosure probe). Batch-46 was then handed the IDENTICAL five components and the IDENTICAL probe. It was not scheduled twice: config.strategy is `oldest_first`, and because batch-45 never stamped components[*].last_checked, all five still read 2026-07-27T04:14:23+02:00 -- twelve days stale -- and were correctly re-selected as the oldest. EVIDENCE: a histogram of components[*].last_checked across all 51 entries runs 2026-07-27 through 2026-08-06 at 5 per day with NO 2026-08-07 bucket at all, while four queue rows carry found_at 2026-08-07; and rotation.next_batch still literally listed the batch-45 five. THIS IS THE CLAUDE.md 'success markers must be written by a reader' FAMILY WITH THE SIGN FLIPPED. The documented failure there is code stamping a success it did not earn -- status=scanned written by a scan that never ran, with the drift watcher then trusting that fabricated freshness. Here nothing false was written; the scan was real and its findings are sound. What went wrong is that the freshness record was not written AT ALL, so the scheduler re-derived work already done. Same root shape either way: the record of what happened is produced separately from the thing that happened, and the two can silently disagree. COST: one wasted batch, and it does not self-correct -- absent this fix batch-47 would have been handed the same five a third time while the 2026-07-28 cohort (infisical, mariadb, qgis_server, redis, rustfs) kept aging unscanned. Note the duplicate was not entirely worthless -- re-probing found the REQUIRE_SIGNIN_VIEW lever that REM-179 had concluded did not exist (REM-180) -- but that is luck, not a reason to re-run batches. FIXED IN THIS BATCH (data only): all five components stamped, rotation.next_batch advanced to the true oldest cohort. SECONDARY, FOUND WHILE FIXING IT: components['postgres'] is a declared ALIAS of components['postgresql'] -- its own notes say so. Because an alias is never itself selected as a batch member it is never stamped, so it ages forever and permanently heads any oldest_first sort, a starvation trap that would hand every future batch a phantom component. Stamped in lockstep with its target here. DURABLE REMEDIATION (NOT applied -- it needs the scanner harness, not a data edit, and a gate you can satisfy by editing the data is not a gate): make the scan-state stamp and the queue append ONE atomic write, so a batch cannot record findings without recording that it ran; and handle alias entries explicitly in the oldest_first selector instead of leaving them in the sort. Filed LOW: it costs duplicated effort and starves coverage rather than exposing the estate -- but starved coverage is how exposure gets missed.

A HEALTHCHECK THAT CANNOT FAIL FOR THE REASON THAT MATTERS. engineering-qgis-server-1 has reported 'healthy' for 3 days and passes the STRICT stack health gate, while the service it fronts does not serve. Measured: the container healthcheck is CMD bash -c ':>/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/80' -- a bare TCP connect that asserts only that Apache accepts a socket. Meanwhile GET / returns an OGC <ServiceExceptionReport> 'Service configuration error / Service unknown or unsupported', and GET /cgi-bin/qgis_mapserv.fcgi returns Apache 404 Not Found even though the binary is present at /usr/lib/cgi-bin/qgis_mapserv.fcgi and ScriptAlias /cgi-bin/ is configured. So no WMS/WFS request can succeed, and nothing in the health signal says so. This is the CLAUDE.md doctrine 'success markers must be written by a reader, not by the attempting code' appearing in the container-health layer: the probe is written by the thing being probed and reads a property (port open) that is not the property anyone cares about (OGC service answers). Note the interaction with REM-184 -- a green health tile is part of why a 2019 image drew no attention. ACTION: replace the TCP-connect healthcheck with a real OGC assertion (a GetCapabilities request whose response must not be a ServiceExceptionReport). Deprioritised behind REM-184 only because fixing the image may replace this container wholesale.

THIRTEEN SECURITY FIXES WITH NO ADVISORY BEHIND THEM. The advisory leg is CLEAN at the pin and was checked authoritatively: the rustfs/rustfs repo security-advisories endpoint returns nothing published after 2026-07-23, and the two advisories of that date -- GHSA-5354-r3w2-34m8 (HIGH, root-parent service account) and GHSA-3ppv-fx5m-m749 (MODERATE, version-specific object reads) -- both name 1.0.0-beta.11 as the patched version, which is what the estate runs (live-verified iiab-rustfs-1 on rustfs/rustfs:1.0.0-beta.11, healthy). So no known-vulnerable version is deployed. The finding is what upstream shipped WITHOUT an advisory. 1.0.0-beta.12 (2026-07-30, 258 changes) carries thirteen explicitly security-labelled commits absent from beta.11, several of which are the same classes this queue has previously received advisories for: 'fix(security): reject federated STS credentials that collide with the root principal' (root-principal collision -- the same escalation class as GHSA-5354, which DID get an advisory), 'fix(authz): fail closed on policy load errors' (fail-open authorization), 'fix(auth): enforce presigned URL expiry limit', 'fix(rpc): authenticate non-disk mutation bodies', 'feat(rpc): add replay-scoped internode authentication', 'fix(security): pin OIDC discovery/token client to the outbound egress policy' (SSRF-class), 'fix(auth): compare sensitive tokens in constant time', 'chore(security): add guardrails against secret values in error strings'. WHY THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN WAVED THROUGH AS FRESHNESS: this vendor has a demonstrated pattern, recorded in REM-139, of publishing advisories that retroactively name a later release as the sole patched version -- there, two advisories landed SEVEN DAYS AFTER a bump and put the freshly-bumped version back at the top of the affected range. Given thirteen unadvised security commits, the probability that some subset is later advisory-backed against beta.11 is material. Deliberately NOT filed HIGH: nothing is currently advisory-backed against the running version, and rating it HIGH would misrepresent the sources. ACTION: bump 1.0.0-beta.11 -> 1.0.0-beta.12 in default.config.yml:2099 (role-default pins were consolidated out, so this is the single declaration). Conservative in-line move; do NOT take 1.0.0-rc.1 (2026-08-08) yet -- it lands a large KMS/SSE rework and an ecstore refactor one day old. install_rustfs=true by default; this one is LIVE. See the REM-059 amendment, which the same bump also advances.  --- SUPERSEDED IN PART 2026-08-10 (cycle-25 batch-48): THE BUMP TARGET IN THIS ROW IS NO LONGER SAFE. Ten hours after this row was written, at 2026-08-09T14:13:50Z, upstream published six advisories; two of them (GHSA-j548-9grx-fh4f HIGH, Object Lock treated as absent on unreadable bucket metadata; GHSA-5w8r-p896-6vq2 HIGH 7.5, OPA plugin omits ExistingObjectTag) declare `<= 1.0.0-beta.12` and therefore name THIS ROW'S RECOMMENDED TARGET as affected, while four more name the running beta.11. This row's own reasoning -- 'this vendor has a demonstrated pattern of publishing advisories that retroactively name a later release as the sole patched version ... the probability that some subset is later advisory-backed against beta.11 is material' -- was correct, and was borne out inside a single day. The thirteen unadvised security commits catalogued here are still the substance; what changed is that beta.12 is no longer the place to land them. FOLLOW REM-189 INSTEAD: the target moves to 1.0.0-rc.1, which all six advisories name as patched, and this row's explicit 'do NOT take 1.0.0-rc.1 yet' is overtaken by that evidence rather than merely disagreed with. Keep this row open as the record of the unadvised-commit leg and close it together with REM-189 and the REM-059 secondary legs on the same bump.

SAME SEMVER, DIFFERENT IMAGE -- BASE-LAYER DRIFT A VERSION PIN CANNOT EXPRESS. The application leg is CLEAN and re-confirmed: MariaDB/server's advisory endpoint shows nothing published after the 2026-06-02 Galera/wsrep wave, every item of which fixes at 11.8.8 (the pin) or below, and 11.8.8 remains the newest 11.8.x on Docker Hub. But the pin names a TAG, and the tag moved underneath it. Local image mariadb:11.8.8 is sha256:efb4959e..., created 2026-07-02. Upstream's arm64 mariadb:11.8.8 is sha256:099e7fa5..., last pushed 2026-08-04. Same MariaDB version, different build -- an official-image rebuild refreshes the Ubuntu noble base layer, so the running container is missing ~33 days of distro security updates that the current tag carries. The container has been up 2 weeks and has never seen the newer build. Nothing in the repo can show this: default.config.yml:1189 says '11.8.8', which is true of both images. This is the cheap, low-stakes instance of the same defect that made REM-184 severe -- there, the frozen base was 7 years old and the vendor was gone; here it is 33 days and one docker pull. Recording both under one lesson: an application-version pin makes NO claim about the userland underneath it, and the estate currently version-scans only the former. ACTION: docker compose pull mariadb + recreate on the next maintenance window; no config change, no migration, same server version. Consider digest-pinning if reproducibility is wanted -- but note REM-184 is what digest-pinning without a freshness check produces.  --- RE-CONFIRMED 2026-08-10 (cycle-25 batch-48): the local half of the drift is unchanged. `docker image inspect mariadb:11.8.8` still reports digest sha256:efb4959ef2c835cd735dbc388eb9ad6aab0c78dd64febcd51bc17481111890c4 created 2026-07-02T02:29:37Z, so no re-pull has happened and the running userland is now ~39 days behind the tag's current build. The upstream arm64 digest could NOT be re-verified this batch -- `docker manifest inspect` hung past timeout against the registry -- so the sha256:099e7fa5 / 2026-08-04 figure carried here is yesterday's measurement, not today's; the local measurement is today's. Independently corroborated by this batch's probe: MariaDB's pre-auth protocol handshake advertises the server version string as `11.8.8-MariaDB-ubu2404`, which names the Ubuntu Noble base image in the same breath as the application version -- a neat demonstration of this row's own point, since the `ubu2404` half is exactly the userland that a pin reading '11.8.8' makes no claim about.

items.finding_ref: GHSA-6r96-hmgc-726c + GHSA-v9cp-qfw9-9pfp + GHSA-j548-9grx-fh4f + GHSA-5w8r-p896-6vq2 + GHSA-x298-9x87-fvjq + GHSA-g3vq-vv42-f647 (six advisories, no CVE ids)
items.remediation_detail: REM-187'S BUMP TARGET IS NOW KNOWN-AFFECTED -- THE PREDICTION IT MADE CAME TRUE IN UNDER 24 HOURS. REM-187 was filed yesterday (2026-08-09T04:12:05+02:00) recording that the rustfs/rustfs advisory endpoint showed nothing published after 2026-07-23, and recommending 1.0.0-beta.11 -> 1.0.0-beta.12 while explicitly advising AGAINST 1.0.0-rc.1 as one day old. That was true when written. At 2026-08-09T14:13:50Z -- about ten hours later -- upstream published SIX advisories at once. FOUR name the running pin beta.11: GHSA-6r96-hmgc-726c (HIGH, CVSS 8.1 AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N, <= beta.11) request headers populate server-derived IAM condition keys -- the condition-value map is built by writing the server-derived request identity first and then folding EVERY remaining request header into the same map; HeaderMap lowercases header names and several server-derived condition keys are lowercase too, so an attacker-chosen header collides by construction, and the collision branch used extend(), appending the caller's value to the trusted vector (sending `userid: admin` makes aws:userid == [real-user, admin], and non-quantified string operators match if ANY element matches); GHSA-v9cp-qfw9-9pfp (HIGH, 8.1, <= beta.11) ForAllValues:/ForAnyValue: combined with a negated string operator evaluate to each other's semantics -- the implementation computes the positive quantified match then negates the aggregate instead of negating the per-value predicate before quantifying, so the two quantifiers are exactly transposed and absent keys are inverted too; GHSA-x298-9x87-fvjq (MEDIUM, 5.3, PR:N/ANONYMOUS, <= beta.11) anonymous ListObjectVersions falls back to re-checking the grant as s3:ListBucket and returns success immediately, skipping deny_anonymous_table_data_plane_if_needed and the RestrictPublicBuckets public-access-block check; GHSA-g3vq-vv42-f647 (MEDIUM, 5.4, <= beta.11) FtpsDriver::mkd() does not authorize s3:CreateBucket before calling storage.create_bucket(), so an authenticated FTP user bypasses the IAM boundary with MKD. TWO MORE REACH BEYOND beta.12, i.e. they name REM-187's recommended target as affected: GHSA-j548-9grx-fh4f (HIGH, <= beta.12) Object Lock (WORM) is treated as ABSENT whenever bucket metadata cannot be read -- the accessors report ConfigNotFound for four distinct realities (genuinely no Object Lock / no readable .metadata.bin / the metadata read faulted / a stored configuration failed to deserialize) and multiple WORM enforcement points collapse all of them into 'not protected', so retained objects including COMPLIANCE-mode ones that BY DESIGN no principal may override are deletable by ordinary DeleteObject/DeleteObjects and by lifecycle sweeps, reported as successful with only a swallowed metadata warning in the logs; and GHSA-5w8r-p896-6vq2 (HIGH, 7.5, >= alpha.64 <= beta.12) the external OPA policy plugin omits existing S3 object tags from authorization requests, so a tagged object is indistinguishable from an untagged one and s3:ExistingObjectTag/* restrictions do not apply. ALL SIX ARE N/A-BY-CONFIG ON THIS DEPLOYMENT, checked against the role rather than assumed: roles/pazny.rustfs/templates/compose.yml.j2 sets exactly two environment variables, RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY and RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY, and a grep across roles/pazny.rustfs/ and files/anatomy/plugins/rustfs-base/ for POLICY_PLUGIN|OBJECT_LOCK|FTP|ANONYMOUS|public.access returns NOTHING. So there is no RUSTFS_POLICY_PLUGIN_URL (GHSA-5w8r inert), no FTP/FTPS frontend (GHSA-g3vq inert, the same disposition that retired CVE-2026-55189), no Object Lock configuration (GHSA-j548 inert), no bucket policy granting anonymous s3:ListBucket (GHSA-x298 inert -- corroborated live: anonymous GET / to the console returns 403 AccessDenied XML), and no IAM policies with condition blocks at all, only the single root credential, so neither header-collision (GHSA-6r96) nor quantified-negation (GHSA-v9cp) has a policy to subvert. FILED MEDIUM, DELIBERATELY NOT HIGH: four upstream-HIGH advisories name the running version, but nothing here is reachable at today's configuration, and rating this HIGH would misrepresent the estate. It is not filed LOW either, because the whole point of REM-187 was that this vendor retroactively re-scopes its affected ranges, and following REM-187 as written would now land the estate on beta.12 -- a version carrying two published HIGH advisories -- while believing itself patched. NOTE THE LATENT TRAP in GHSA-j548 specifically: nOS uses RustFS as the nightly backup target, and Object Lock is exactly the hardening an operator would reach for to make backups immutable; enabling it on beta.11/beta.12 would produce documented WORM protection that silently does not hold whenever bucket metadata is unreadable. ACTION: the fix target CHANGES from REM-187's 1.0.0-beta.12 to 1.0.0-rc.1 (2026-08-08), which every one of the six names as the patched version (GHSA-j548 verbatim: 'Fixed in 1.0.0-rc.1 by PR #5648. Upgrade to 1.0.0-rc.1 or later.'). This SUPERSEDES REM-187's explicit 'do NOT take 1.0.0-rc.1 yet' -- that caution was sound on the evidence available yesterday and is simply overtaken: rc.1 is now the ONLY release clear of all six. Because nothing is reachable, this is a supervised maintenance bump, not an urgent one; rc.1 does land a large KMS/SSE rework and an ecstore refactor, so verify the container reads existing data and /health returns ready before declaring success. Single declaration at default.config.yml:2127 (role-default pins were consolidated out). install_rustfs=true by default and this one is LIVE. METHOD NOTE, unchanged and re-confirmed: OSV's crates.io index is incomplete for RustFS and none of these six carry a CVE id, so only the rustfs/rustfs GitHub security-advisories endpoint surfaces them; it was read directly.

THE PROBE'S FINDING OF RECORD, AND IT OVERTURNS A STANDING DISPOSITION. Every rustfs entry since batch-36 has asserted that 'the pre-auth leg is CLOSED at this pin', reasoning that the S3 and admin APIs host-bind 127.0.0.1:9010 loopback and that only the console is edge-published. The loopback half is true. The conclusion is not: https://fs.pazny.eu/health returns HTTP 200 anonymously with {"status":"ok","ready":true,"service":"rustfs-endpoint","timestamp":"...","version":"1.0.0-beta.11"} -- the exact prerelease version, unauthenticated, in the body. INTERNET REACH IS CONFIRMED, NOT INFERRED, and this is the part that separates this row from REM-144's careful hedge. REM-144 could only claim LAN/Tailscale reach because split-horizon dnsmasq resolved its 'public' test back to the host's own LAN address, so the request provably never left the network. Here the test was re-run against the PUBLIC Cloudflare anycast address explicitly (curl --resolve fs.pazny.eu:443:188.114.96.9, the address 1.1.1.1 returns) and the response carried server: cloudflare, cf-ray: a28b78ef5f4c90a2-PRG and cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC. A cf-ray stamped at the Prague PoP with DYNAMIC (i.e. not served from cache) proves the request traversed the real Cloudflare edge and was forwarded to this origin. Anyone on the internet can read this host's exact RustFS version. WHY THE EDGE DOES NOT STOP IT: traefik_auth_modes['rustfs']='none' (roles/pazny.traefik/vars/main.yml:41, comment 'S3 API, own credentials'), so the auto-derived router carries NO authentik@file middleware. This is precisely the batch-38 lesson restated -- 'oidc' means the edge is open and the app's own login is the only gate; 'none' means the edge is open and there is no gate at all. RustFS's own authorization is in fact doing the work almost everywhere, which is why this is MEDIUM and not worse: an anonymous sweep of the edge returns 403 AccessDenied for /, /version, /rustfs/admin/v3/info, /api/v1/version, /static/index.html and /login, with only /health (200, version-bearing) and /favicon.ico (200) answering. So the correct statement is not 'the pre-auth leg is closed' but 'the pre-auth leg is narrowed to two endpoints, one of which publishes the version'. WHY A VERSION STRING IS WORTH A ROW FOR THIS COMPONENT SPECIFICALLY, rather than the usual shrug at banner disclosure: RustFS is a prerelease-cadence vendor that assigns NO CVE ids and has now twice published advisories that retroactively name a later release as the sole patched version (REM-139, where two advisories landed seven days after a bump and put the freshly-bumped version back at the top of the affected range; and REM-189, where six landed ten hours after REM-187 recorded the advisory leg clean). An anonymous reader of /health today learns that this host runs beta.11, against which four advisories were published on 2026-08-09 -- including two rated 8.1. Those four are N/A-by-config here (see REM-189), so this is disclosure of an accurate targeting signal rather than of a live hole; that is exactly why it is MEDIUM rather than HIGH, and why it should not be dismissed as LOW either. ACTION, two independent halves. (1) The version field: RustFS's /health is also the container healthcheck target (compose.yml.j2 healthcheck wget's http://127.0.0.1:9000/health) and state/manifest.yml's health probe, so it must keep answering on loopback -- the fix is not to remove it but to stop publishing it anonymously at the edge. (2) The edge posture, which is the durable half: flip traefik_auth_modes['rustfs'] from 'none' to 'proxy' so authentik@file gates fs.<tld>, or drop rustfs's domain_var from the manifest entirely if no human needs the console from a browser. Prior rustfs entries have floated 'optionally flip the console router to proxy' as defence-in-depth since 2026-07-01; this row is the evidence that it is not optional. VERIFY BEFORE MERGING that no S3 client reaches RustFS through the edge hostname -- the backup path uses the loopback API port and should be unaffected, but a forward-auth gate would 302 any machine caller that does.

items.remediation_detail: FIRST-EVER default_credentials_test probe run (attack_probe_schedule cycle_mod 2, last_run was null). THE FINDING: Superset's highest-privilege account is a LOCAL Flask-AppBuilder DB user named `admin`, created every converge by `superset fab create-admin --username admin --password {{ superset_admin_password }}` (roles/pazny.superset/tasks/post.yml:43-52). superset_admin_password defaults to `{{ global_password_prefix }}_pw_superset` (default.config.yml:2265) and is NOT overridden in the operator's config.yml/credentials.yml, so the live value is prefix-derived (`<prefix>_pw_superset`). It is NOT in main.yml's lazy-regenerate group (verified: the block at main.yml:1406-1500 rescues outline/paperclip/etc. but has no superset_* entry), so unlike those it stays concatenation-derived at runtime -- squarely inside the REM-144 blast radius (one leaked sibling credential reveals the master prefix, and the master yields this by construction). WHY THE INTENDED OIDC-ONLY GATE DOES NOT HOLD: the config sets AUTH_TYPE=AUTH_OAUTH (superset_config.py.j2), which the estate treats as 'native OIDC handles login' -- and traefik_auth_modes['superset']='oidc' (roles/pazny.traefik/vars/main.yml) therefore attaches NO authentik@file forward-auth middleware to the auto-derived edge router (manifest id superset has domain_var+port_var, state/manifest.yml:746-756). But Flask-AppBuilder's SecurityApi login endpoint `POST /api/v1/security/login` accepts an explicit `{"provider":"db"}` and authenticates against the LOCAL user table regardless of AUTH_TYPE -- so the OIDC front door is bypassed entirely by the DB-auth API. PROVEN LIVE (not inferred): `curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8089/api/v1/security/login -d '{"username":"admin","password":"<wrong>","provider":"db"}'` returns HTTP 401 {"message":"Not authorized"} -- a credential EVALUATION-and-rejection, not a 404 or 'provider disabled', confirming the db-auth path is live under AUTH_OAUTH. (No attempt was made with the real derived password -- account access would be exfiltration; the wrong-password 401 is sufficient proof.) INTERNET REACH CONFIRMED to REM-190's standard: curl --resolve superset.pazny.eu:443:188.114.96.9 https://superset.pazny.eu/ returned HTTP 302 -> /superset/welcome/ with server: cloudflare, cf-ray: a293af8efd7f58b7-PRG (Prague PoP), cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC -- the request traversed the real Cloudflare edge to this origin (a plain local curl hit gunicorn directly via split-horizon dnsmasq, the REM-144/190 caveat; the forced-anycast test defeats it). IMPACT: anyone on the internet who learns/guesses `<prefix>_pw_superset` gets Superset Admin, i.e. SQLLab arbitrary SQL against every connected database -- a data-plane compromise, not just a dashboard. The operator prefix is a low-entropy human string, and the same password is not shared with siblings only by luck of the `_pw_superset` suffix -- any ONE sibling leak still yields the prefix. REMEDIATION (defense-in-depth, in priority order): (1) set superset_admin_password to a minted random secret (add to main.yml lazy-regenerate group, mirroring paperclip_auth_secret) so it leaves the prefix blast radius; (2) disable local DB login under OAuth -- set FAB `AUTH_USER_REGISTRATION`/db-provider off is insufficient, the SecurityApi db path needs the local admin's password rotated to random AND ideally the account demoted/removed once OIDC admin mapping (AUTH_ROLES_MAPPING nos-admins->Admin) is confirmed working; (3) if a break-glass local admin must persist, gate the edge router with forward_auth too (accepting the documented double-login) OR bind superset off the public edge. Structural root cause is shared with REM-192 (freescout): 'oidc' in traefik_auth_modes means THE EDGE IS OPEN and the app's own login is the only gate -- and here that gate is a prefix-derived default credential.  ||  MITIGATED IN THE REPO 2026-08-11 (converge pending), and the row is deliberately NOT closed on the bypass itself. WHAT WAS AND WAS NOT FIXED. NOT fixed: the endpoint. Flask-AppBuilder's POST /api/v1/security/login dispatches {"provider":"db"} straight to auth_user_db() with no reference to AUTH_TYPE -- read in the INSTALLED flask_appbuilder/security/api.py inside data-superset-1, not inferred from docs -- and FAB exposes no setting that disables it. There is nothing to configure. FIXED: what made that endpoint dangerous rather than merely present. superset_admin_password was `{global_password_prefix}_pw_superset`, so one leaked sibling credential yields it by construction (REM-144). It now joins main.yml's lazy-regenerate group (`'_pw_' in value` -> openssl rand -base64 24) and templates/secrets.yml.j2 persists it. THE HALF THAT IS EASY TO GET WRONG, and a gate caught the first attempt: `fab create-admin` on an EXISTING user leaves the password untouched, so regenerating the variable alone would have updated ~/.nos/secrets.yml and left the live account still answering to the derived value -- a fix visible everywhere except where it matters. roles/pazny.superset/tasks/post.yml now runs `fab reset-password` and, because that carries failed_when:false to keep a converge alive, an assert REFUSES a silent reset failure by name. A SECOND gate (test_minted_secrets_are_persisted) then refused the change until the new secret was persisted -- without that, every converge would mint a different password and dutifully apply it. WHAT REMAINS OPEN, and why the row stays: an internet-reachable password endpoint on a Tier-2 service. It is now guarded by a random 24-byte secret instead of a derived one, which is ordinary rather than alarming, but the OIDC-only claim in this estate's SSO trichotomy is still false for superset. Closing that means either edge forward-auth (traefik_auth_modes['superset'] = 'proxy', at the cost of the documented double-login for a genuinely native_oidc service) or an upstream FAB switch that does not exist. That is an operator decision, not a side effect of a credential change. VERIFY AFTER THE NEXT CONVERGE: the OLD derived password must be REJECTED -- curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8089/api/v1/security/login -d '{"username":"admin","password":"<prefix>_pw_superset","provider":"db"}' must return 401, and the value in ~/.nos/secrets.yml must return 200.

items.remediation_detail: default_credentials_test probe (first run). THE FINDING OVERTURNS FreeScout's own auth classification. traefik_auth_modes['freescout']='oidc' (roles/pazny.traefik/vars/main.yml) asserts 'native OIDC handles login', so the auto-derived edge router (manifest freescout has domain_var+port_var, state/manifest.yml:621-629) carries NO authentik@file forward-auth middleware. But FreeScout's native OIDC DOES NOT EXIST on this estate: the freescout-oauth module never installs -- both upstream sources are HTTP 404 (freescout-help-desk/oauth, tiredofit/freescout-module-oauth), documented at length in roles/pazny.freescout/tasks/post.yml. So /login renders ONLY the local email+password form and no 'Sign in with Authentik' button -- the 'oidc' gate is imaginary and the edge is simply OPEN onto a local-credential form. PROVEN LIVE: curl -H 'Host: helpdesk.pazny.eu' http://127.0.0.1:8090/login (following the 302->https) returns HTTP 200 with name="email"+name="password" input fields and NO oauth/authentik markers. THE CREDENTIAL: the admin account is admin@pazny.eu (freescout_admin_email = default_admin_email, default.config.yml:2188/122), seeded + password-reconverged every run via artisan (post.yml), with freescout_admin_password defaulting to `{{ global_password_prefix }}_pw_freescout` (default.credentials.yml:259-260), NOT overridden by the operator and NOT lazy-regenerated -- prefix-derived at runtime, inside the REM-144 blast radius. INTERNET REACH CONFIRMED (REM-190 standard): curl --resolve helpdesk.pazny.eu:443:188.114.96.9 https://helpdesk.pazny.eu/ returned HTTP 302 -> /login with server: cloudflare, cf-ray: a293af8e8be023fa-PRG, cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC -- real Cloudflare edge to this origin. IMPACT: anyone on the internet who learns/guesses `<prefix>_pw_freescout` gets FreeScout admin -- full read/write over a helpdesk holding customer PII and inbound mail, plus module/agent management. REMEDIATION: (1) mint freescout_admin_password random + persist (leave the prefix blast radius); (2) the honest fix for the classification lie is to FLIP traefik_auth_modes['freescout'] to 'proxy' so the edge forward-auth-gates it -- FreeScout has no working native OIDC, so 'oidc' is wrong today and 'proxy' matches reality (a browser SSO gate in front of the local form is NOT a double-login here, because there is no second login). Re-evaluate 'oidc' only if/when a reachable freescout-oauth module source is supplied. Shares its structural root cause with REM-191 (superset).

items.resolved_by: RECLASSIFIED native_oidc -> forward_auth, 2026-08-11, in the repo (converge pending). The row's finding stands entirely: `oidc` asserted that FreeScout's own login page gates the user, so the auto-derived Traefik router carried no authentik@file middleware, while the freescout-oauth module never installs (both upstream sources HTTP 404) and /login served a bare local email+password form at an internet-facing edge. THE FIX IS THE CLASSIFICATION, not a module hunt: docs/active-work.md already carried the decision ('find a reachable module source, OR reclassify FreeScout as forward_auth') and the probe settled which branch to take. Changed: files/anatomy/plugins/freescout-base/plugin.yml mode+provider_type -> forward_auth with redirect_uris and scopes REMOVED (a proxy provider has no OIDC client, and leaving them declares a callback nothing can reach); roles/pazny.traefik/vars/main.yml traefik_auth_modes.freescout -> `proxy`; state/tofu-authentik-services.yml regenerated (freescout now mode: forward_auth, client_secret and redirect_uris dropped). TWO THINGS WORTH RECORDING FOR THE NEXT READER. (1) The first attempt set the traefik map to `forward_auth` — the DOCTRINE word — and tests/anatomy/test_access_facet_reconciled.py caught it: that map's vocabulary is proxy|oidc|none, and an unrecognised value would have left the route ungated while every document said otherwise. (2) The MTI provider-flip trap (a stale OAuth2Provider blocking the new ProxyProvider on the shared Provider base row) does NOT apply here: authentik_engine resolves to `tofu` via config.yml, where proxy and oauth2 are distinct typed resources. Verified with tools/estate-status.py --config authentik_engine, because default.config.yml alone says `blueprint`. VERIFY AFTER THE NEXT CONVERGE: an unauthenticated GET to the FreeScout host must 302 to auth.<tld>, not 200 with a password form.

items.remediation_detail: Cycle-27 batch-50 ATTACK PROBE (2026-08-12, ssrf_vector_analysis) -- LIVE-CONFIRMED end to end, and it is the probe's finding of record. It is a NEW finding, distinct from REM-144 (resolved), whose `resolved_by` explicitly reasoned the :8080 dashboard was safe because 'the compose override binds it to 127.0.0.1 only'. That reasoning is INCOMPLETE: the `127.0.0.1:{{traefik_dashboard_port}}:8080` map in roles/pazny.traefik/templates/compose.yml.j2:20 constrains only HOST callers. Traefik's api.insecure=true (traefik.yml.j2:11) opens the built-in 'traefik' entrypoint on :8080 bound to 0.0.0.0 INSIDE the container, and the container joins infra_net + shared_net (compose.yml.j2:30-31, traefik_networks default) plus gated_net + gated_b2b_net. So every one of the ~40 peer containers on those flat networks reaches http://infra-traefik-1:8080/ UNAUTHENTICATED by container DNS name. PROVEN: `docker exec iiab-uptime-kuma-1 node -e 'http.get(infra-traefik-1:8080/api/overview)'` returns 200 with the full router/service/middleware topology (recon of every backend). THE ESCALATION: GET /api/http/middlewares returns the file-provider `headers` middlewares VERBATIM, including the two customRequestHeaders that carry the edge ANTI-SPOOF secrets in plaintext -- face-edge@file -> X-Face-Edge-Token and wing-edge@file -> X-Wing-Edge-Token (roles/pazny.traefik/templates/dynamic/middlewares.yml.j2:80,92). These tokens are the ENTIRE anti-spoof gate: Wing BasePresenter::enforceEdgeTrust() and the Face BFF trust forged X-Authentik-* identity headers ONLY on requests carrying the matching token (the 'request passed through the edge' proof). LIVE EXPLOIT CHAIN, all three legs measured: (1) any shared_net peer reads both tokens off :8080 anonymously; (2) a gated_net peer (calibre-web -- it shares gated_net with face-1) replays the stolen X-Face-Edge-Token + forged `X-Authentik-Username: admin` + `X-Authentik-Groups: nos-providers,nos-admins` to http://iiab-face-1:5090/ -> HTTP 200 (authenticated as Tier-1 admin); (3) controls hold -- no token = 403, wrong token = 403. So the leaked secret is sufficient to forge Tier-1 identity into Face. The Wing leg is narrower: Wing runs host launchd on 127.0.0.1:9000 (not on any docker network), so a container cannot reach it directly -- the leaked X-Wing-Edge-Token is only weaponizable from a host-level foothold, but it is still exposed to the whole container fabric. NOT anonymous-from-internet (needs one container foothold), hence HIGH not CRITICAL -- but it is precisely the SSRF-amplification the probe hunts: any container-scoped SSRF sink (uptime-kuma admin-monitor SSRF REM-044, vaultwarden icon SSRF REM-136, a compromised low-value service) pivots to :8080 to harvest the identity-forgery keys, and the flat shared_net (40+ members, SEC-02 only isolated calibre/2fauth/firefly) is the amplifier. REMEDIATION OPTIONS (any one closes it): (a) drop api.insecure and publish the dashboard via a loopback-only router/entrypoint the peer network cannot address; (b) add a dedicated internal entrypoint bound to the host-gateway/127.0.0.1 for :8080 and take traefik off shared_net for the dashboard; (c) stop shipping the edge tokens as a plaintext customRequestHeaders middleware the API reflects -- move edge-trust to an IP-allowlist or a middleware whose secret the /api does not echo. Verify after fix: `docker exec <any shared_net peer> wget -qO- http://infra-traefik-1:8080/api/http/middlewares` must fail to connect (or must not contain X-*-Edge-Token).

items.resolved_by: FIXED + LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-08-12. Root cause was api.insecure:true (roles/pazny.traefik/templates/traefik.yml.j2): the built-in traefik entrypoint served the WHOLE unauthenticated API on container :8080 (0.0.0.0), reachable by every peer container by DNS name. FIX: (1) api.insecure=false so the API leaves :8080 entirely; (2) a dedicated `ping` entrypoint on :8080 serving ONLY /ping (harmless liveness) so the host publish + container healthcheck + nos-smoke /ping keep working; (3) the dashboard moves to an OPT-IN SSO-gated api@internal router (authentik@file, websecure), default OFF (traefik_dashboard_route_enabled) because `traefik` has no Authentik provider yet so the route would 404 — it fails closed. LIVE PROOF (docker exec iiab-uptime-kuma-1 node http.get infra-traefik-1:8080): /api/overview 200->404, /api/http/middlewares 200->404 with NO Edge-Token in body (was 'LEAK: Edge-Token present'), /ping still 200 'OK' from BOTH a peer and host 127.0.0.1:8082. Gate: tests/anatomy/test_traefik_api_not_insecure.py (insecure:false, ping entrypoint, dashboard route api@internal+authentik@file if present). items.remediation_detail: Cycle-27 batch-50 CVE scan (2026-08-12). CONTEXT OVERTURN: janeczku/calibre-web shipped 0.6.27 ('Ludmila') on 2026-08-08 -- 9 days after the last calibre-web look -- and it is a SECURITY release. This retires the 'janeczku dormant / no upstream fix exists' disposition that BOTH REM-074 (resolved) and REM-120 (resolved) rest on: REM-074 closed CVE-2025-6998 (ReDoS in strip_whitespaces) on the theory the fix lived only in the Autocaliweb fork, and REM-120 closed the Kobo-token IDOR (CVE-2026-7709 class) saying 'NO janeczku fix exists, vendor unresponsive'. The 0.6.27 release notes' Security section explicitly fixes BOTH -- 'ReDoS vulnerability in whitespace stripping is now fixed (CVE-2025-6998)' and 'IDOR in Kobo tokens is now fixed' -- plus a cluster more: 'External binary names now restricted to prevent remote command execution (CVE-2025-7404)' (the OS-command-injection assessed-not-queued in REM-074's tail), SQL injection via the database path parameter, LDAP injection in bind_user/get_object_details, XXE in EPUB/FB2/Goodreads parsing, two stored-XSS (book comments + author names), unauthorized /show/ book-file access, and encryption-key file perms 0o600. The 0.6.26..0.6.27 compare is 135 commits touching cps/kobo_auth.py, cps/admin.py, cps/editbooks.py, cps/helper.py, cps/string_helper.py, and a new cps/binary_helper.py -- consistent with the advertised fixes. The LSIO image is already published (Docker Hub linuxserver/calibre-web:0.6.27 and 0.6.27-ls395, 2026-08-09T02:39Z, arm64v8 tag present). PERIMETER (unchanged, still mitigating): calibre_web is forward_auth (authentik@file wall), 127.0.0.1:8083 loopback, and SEC-02 gated_net-only -- so these are authenticated/insider-scoped, not anonymous. But several fixed bugs (Kobo IDOR, /show/ unauthorized access, stored XSS) are exploitable by any authenticated Tier-3 SSO user against another, and the pin now demonstrably lags a real fix rather than facing an unmaintained upstream -- so this is an actionable HIGH version bump, not an accept-with-doc. REMEDIATION: repin calibreweb_version 0.6.26 -> 0.6.27 in default.config.yml:1773 (NOTE the 0.6.27 upgrade REQUIRES the nh3 lib in place of deprecated bleach -- the LSIO image bundles it, but verify the container starts clean post-bump). NOTE also this is the ideal moment to reconsider REM-074/REM-120's 'migrate to a fork' advice -- staying on maintained janeczku 0.6.27 is now viable.

items.remediation_detail: Cycle-28 batch-51 CVE scan (2026-08-13). NEW CRITICAL, published 2026-08-11, two days before this scan. CVE-2026-19516 (CVSS 9.1, CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:L, grafana.com/security/security-advisories/cve-2026-19516/): an authenticated caller invoking the `grafana_api_request` tool controls the X-Grafana-URL header and thereby the OUTBOUND request destination, and READS THE RESPONSE -- internal networks, loopback, and cloud metadata endpoints. This is the SECOND bite at the same header. Grafana's own advisory states the CVE-2026-15583 patch (REM-150) 'prevented token leakage but failed to restrict destination targeting entirely'. Fix floor moves 0.17.1 -> 1.1.0. APPLICABILITY -- AFFECTED, measured not inferred: `docker ps` shows iiab-mcp-grafana-1 live; the image's OCI revision label resolves to commit 76ed7db (2026-07-07), which GitHub compare places 1 commit BEHIND v0.17.1 and 27 commits behind v1.1.0. So the resident binary predates BOTH fixes. The pin is a DIGEST pin (mcp_grafana_version: 'latest@sha256:9362bcf...'), i.e. the estate is deliberately frozen to a pre-fix build -- a re-pull cannot rescue it, and would not help anyway because Docker Hub mcp/grafana has published nothing since 2026-07-08. THE REMEDIATION IS BLOCKED ON REGISTRY AVAILABILITY, which is the honest finding here: the fixed version exists in source (grafana/mcp-grafana v1.1.0) but not on the registry this role consumes. ghcr.io/grafana/mcp-grafana returns HTTP 403 to anonymous manifest requests for every tag tried (v1.1.0, 1.1.0, v0.17.2, latest) -- that is access-denied, NOT proof of absence, and must be re-checked with credentials before concluding anything. Options, in order: (a) authenticate to ghcr and repin to v1.1.0 if the tag is there; (b) build from source (Go, Apache-2.0) and pin a local image; (c) if neither, DISABLE the mcp-grafana backend -- an unfixable SSRF-to-metadata sink holding a Grafana service-account token is not worth its convenience. PERIMETER (mitigating, unchanged from REM-150, and why an operator should not panic): `docker port` shows 8000/tcp -> null (no host publish); mcp-grafana is absent from state/manifest.yml so Traefik derives NO router; the fronting mcpo is forward-auth gated (traefik_auth_modes.mcp_gateway='proxy') AND --api-key protected. PR:L in the vector means the attacker must already be an authenticated MCP caller. So the realistic path is a foothold on iiab_net / the flat shared_net -- the same amplifier REM-194 documents -- not an anonymous internet request. Filed CRITICAL on the CVSS and on S:C (scope change) + the service-account token it holds (GRAFANA_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN, roles/pazny.mcp_gateway/templates/compose.yml.j2:71, populated by tasks/post.yml:108); the perimeter is what keeps it off the 'live-exploitable today' list.
items.resolved_by: CONVERGED AND LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-08-13. Resident digest is now sha256:f21a19cebbfa7c3a76ef1746171e5ffc3601064e432f593e7c6cb526e5216e5f (grafana/mcp-grafana:1.1.0), measured with `docker inspect iiab-mcp-grafana-1` and byte-identical to the pin -- above BOTH the 0.17.1 (REM-150) and 1.1.0 (REM-196) floors; v1.1.0 removes the X-Grafana-URL header outright. All three fixed; `POST /grafana/check_datasources_health` now returns OK for all five datasources and 65 tools are mounted.
