items.remediation_detail: Cycle-28 batch-51 PROBE finding of record (docker_escape_paths, 2026-08-13). The grafana role's compose template renders more than Grafana: the exporter fleet at its tail includes cAdvisor, and cAdvisor is the single highest-privilege container in the estate. Measured, all of it: `privileged: true`; runs as uid 0 (the other four components in this batch all run non-root -- authentik 1000, grafana 472, loki 10001, kiwix 'user'); SecurityOpt [label=disable]; host `/` bind-mounted at /rootfs; /sys, /var/lib/docker and /var/run bound; and it joins observability_net AND the flat `shared_net` alongside ~40 peers. THE SOCKET IS LIVE, and this took proving because the surface lies twice. First lie: `ls -l` inside the container shows /var/run/docker.sock as a SYMLINK to /Users/pazny/.docker/run/docker.sock -- the `/var/run:/var/run:ro` bind shadows the explicit socket bind and drags in the macOS host's /var/run (Apple's own sockets are visible in there). That reads like a dangling link. It is not: /proc/self/mountinfo line 2004 shows `/host-services/docker.proxy.sock -> /Users/pazny/.docker/run/docker.sock` on tmpfs, i.e. the symlink resolves THROUGH a real bind of Docker Desktop's live API socket, and `cat` on it returns ENXIO ('No such device or address' = it IS a socket) rather than ENOENT. Second lie: `:ro` on a unix-socket bind is cosmetic. It prevents unlinking the socket FILE; it does not make the Docker API read-only, because the API is a request/response protocol over that socket. Any code execution inside cAdvisor is therefore host root: POST /containers/create with Privileged:true and Binds:['/:/host']. `docker info` confirms no rootless mode and no Enhanced Container Isolation (SecurityOptions = seccomp builtin + cgroupns only), so nothing upstream of the socket constrains that call. WHAT IT BUYS, MEASURED -- and this is the part that decides the remediation: essentially nothing on this platform. Prometheus holds ONE series for container_cpu_usage_seconds_total and ONE for container_memory_usage_bytes, both labelled id='/' (the root cgroup) -- there are NO per-container CPU or memory metrics at all, which is cAdvisor's entire reason to exist. /api/v1.3/docker returns 0 containers. The container log is an endless repeat of 'Failed to create existing container ... failed to identify the read-write layer ID ... open /rootfs/var/lib/docker/image/overlayfs/layerdb/mounts/<id>/mount-id: no such file or directory' -- because on Docker Desktop for Mac, /rootfs is the macOS filesystem while the real /var/lib/docker lives inside the LinuxKit VM. cAdvisor is architecturally unable to do its job here. So the estate is paying maximum privilege (root + full Docker API + host rootfs + label=disable) for a component returning one root-cgroup series and a log-spam loop. The 85 container_fs_usage_bytes series are host filesystem devices, not containers. EXPLOITABILITY, rated honestly: EXPLOITABLE-POST-FOOTHOLD, not remotely triggerable. cAdvisor's :8080 answers HTTP 200 unauthenticated (both /api/v1.3/containers and the /containers/ UI) and is reachable by DNS name from every shared_net peer -- the identical mistake REM-194 documents for Traefik, since `127.0.0.1:8080` is a HOST firewall and never a container-network one -- but that API is read-only metrics and leaks no secret, and no CVE or public RCE exists against cAdvisor. So the vector needs code execution in the cAdvisor process; what the finding establishes is that the blast radius of ANY such bug is host root, and that this is being carried for zero delivered value. It also makes cAdvisor the most valuable pivot target on shared_net for the SSRF chains already queued (REM-044, REM-136, REM-194). REMEDIATION, in preference order: (a) DROP cAdvisor on Darwin -- gate the service block and alloy_scrape_cadvisor on `ansible_os_family != 'Darwin'`; it works on the Linux port, where the cgroup and layerdb paths are real, and delivers nothing on macOS; (b) if it must stay, route it through the docker-socket-proxy the estate ALREADY runs for exactly this purpose (roles/pazny.portainer + roles/pazny.traefik use `--host tcp://docker-socket-proxy:2375`, which is how REM-001 and REM-002 were closed) and drop `privileged: true`, the `/` and `/var/run` binds, and `label=disable`; (c) at minimum take it off shared_net. Bumping v0.49.1 -> v0.60.5 is worth doing for hygiene but fixes NONE of this -- the privilege is in our compose file, not in their release notes. VERIFY: `docker inspect observability-cadvisor-1 --format '{{.HostConfig.Privileged}}'` must be false, and `docker exec observability-cadvisor-1 stat /var/run/docker.sock` must not resolve to a socket. PRECEDENT, shipped ONE DAY before this scan: REM-194 was closed 2026-08-12 by setting api.insecure=false so Traefik's API left container :8080 and only a /ping entrypoint remains there. That fix accepted exactly the principle this finding rests on -- a loopback host-map does not gate the container fabric, and an unauthenticated :8080 on shared_net is a finding even when the host binding looks safe. cAdvisor is the same shape, on the same network, still open. Whoever fixed REM-194 has already agreed with the reasoning; this is the second instance of it, and the one with host-root on the other side of the socket.

items.remediation_detail: Cycle-29 batch-52 CVE scan (2026-08-14). NEW CRITICAL, published 2026-08-11T19:19:08Z -- three days before this scan, and it lands on a pin that was CORRECT when it was set. This is the fourth Metabase finding in the queue and the SECOND to arrive with NO CVE ID (cve_id: null), so the methodology note attached to REM-153 keeps earning its place: api.github.com/repos/metabase/metabase/security-advisories is the only channel that shows it. A CVE-keyed feed sees nothing. VERSION MAPPING: Metabase writes advisory ranges as `x.NN.P` covering BOTH the OSS 0.x and the EE 1.x builds, so the pin v0.63.5 reads directly as x.63.5. The affected range is >= x.63.0, < x.63.10 -> AFFECTED, by five patch releases. WHAT IT IS: GHSA-r495-55cx-fjh7, 'Multiple vulnerabilities across query validation, permissions, and network exposure' -- an upstream hardening ROLL-UP of ten distinct issue classes, published as one critical advisory with no per-issue severities: (1) SQL-injection hardening -- query parameters, filters, cast options and metric/segment definitions lacked strict validation, so user-supplied values could reach the database as raw SQL rather than as data; (2) a HoneySQL dependency bump to pick up CVE-2026-61620 in the SQL-generation library -- the ONE identifier in the whole advisory, and it is a transitive one; (3) incomplete permission checks on cards, dashboards and actions, with nested question references and dashboard-card additions bypassing the check entirely; (4) rate-limit bypass via request-header manipulation on the login AND password-reset endpoints; (5) a version-revert authorization gap that could restore sensitive settings without revalidating permissions; (6) sandboxing-integrity issues letting crafted requests bypass row/column-level restrictions and impersonation controls; (7) loose API request validation; (8) network exposure via legacy HTTP action execution, SSH-tunnel binding and unauthenticated site-URL influence; (9) administrative access control gaps in public question sharing, database health checks and settings management; (10) client-overrideable query and download row limits. SEVERITY, ARGUED RATHER THAN COPIED: upstream's own label is Critical and this batch keeps it, but for a narrower reason than the two August CVEs it follows. Nothing here is stated to be unauthenticated-RCE and nothing is stated to be under active exploitation -- that was GHSA-vwf4-m7j8-wcjf (CVE-2026-72898, CVSS 10.0, '/api/session/reset_password', 'Metabase has confirmed active exploitation'), which the current pin ALREADY covers (fix x.63.5). What carries the CRITICAL here is item (1) plus item (8): an injection-hardening roll-up on a product whose entire purpose is to accept operator-authored queries, on an instance where -- per docs/sso-and-attribution.md -- Metabase OSS has no OIDC and therefore sits behind a Traefik forward_auth gate in front of ONE SHARED account. Every tenant user who clears the Authentik wall is the same query-capable principal, so 'authenticated-only' buys much less separation here than it would on an instance with per-user Metabase accounts, and the audit trail cannot attribute the query to a person either. SCOPED HONESTLY -- what is NOT true of this estate: public sharing is the precondition for several of the recent Metabase criticals, and the live instance currently has no publicly shared cards or dashboards, no external database attached (the only entry in metabase_database is id=1 'Sample Database', engine=sqlite, read-only), and site-url pointing at loopback. So the reachable blast radius today is the Metabase application database itself, not a warehouse. That is an argument about EXPOSURE, not about the fix: the roll-up is still five patch releases of unpatched hardening on the estate's only BI surface. CORRECTION OF RECORD, filed here because it changes how a future reader weighs REM-153: that item justified its CRITICAL partly with 'the bundled SAMPLE DATABASE IS H2, so no operator has to attach an H2 source for the primitive to exist'. On this estate at v0.63.5 that is measurably not the case -- `SELECT engine FROM metabase_database` returns `sqlite`, with details {"db":"/plugins/sample-database.sqlite","read-only?":true}. REM-153 is resolved by version regardless, so nothing re-opens; but the 'H2 by default' premise should not be carried forward into a future H2-family finding without re-measuring the engine column first. ACTION: bump metabase_version to v0.63.10 in default.config.yml:2270 (single declaration -- the role-default shadow was removed 2026-08-05) and converge with `--tags metabase`, which per A17 re-renders the override AND recreates data-metabase-1. The 0.63 line is a patch bump, so no upgrade recipe and no Flyway major-migration risk; expect the usual 5-10 minute first-boot health window the compose healthcheck already budgets for (start_period 300s).

items.current_version: v0.63.5 -- configuration finding, version-independent. roles/pazny.metabase/templates/compose.yml.j2 environment block + files/anatomy/plugins/metabase-base/templates/metabase-base.compose.yml.j2 (identity-only).
items.fix_version: config_change: set MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY (>= 16 chars) from a generated secret, and re-key existing rows once with `java -jar metabase.jar rotate-encryption-key` if any secret already exists.
items.remediation_detail: Cycle-29 batch-52 ATTACK PROBE (tls_crypto_weakness). MEASURED, not inferred: `docker exec data-metabase-1 env | grep -c MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY` returns 0, and a repo-wide grep for MB_ENCRYPTION / metabase_encryption returns nothing -- the variable exists in neither the role compose template nor the metabase-base plugin compose-extension. Metabase's at-rest encryption of application-database secrets is therefore OFF, which is upstream's default. WHAT THAT ACTUALLY ENCRYPTS, stated precisely because the name over-promises: MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY encrypts the `details` column of metabase_database (connected-database connection strings and credentials), stored integration secrets, and a handful of settings values. It is not full-database encryption and it is not transport security. WHY THIS IS FILED AT MEDIUM AND NOT HIGHER -- the honest scoping, which a future reader should re-measure rather than inherit: the blast radius today is EMPTY. `SELECT id, name, engine, details FROM metabase_database` on the live app DB returns exactly one row -- the read-only sqlite Sample Database -- so there are currently no warehouse credentials to leak in cleartext. The finding is that the estate has no gate stopping the first real data source from being attached into cleartext storage, and that the moment an operator connects one (which is the entire point of running Metabase), the Postgres row holding those credentials is readable by anything that can read the `metabase` database in infra-postgresql-1 -- including a nightly backup artifact and any peer with the metabase DB password. UPSTREAM MAKES THE SAME LINK, which is what promoted this from a checklist item to a filed row: GHSA-8hmm-hrhg-ppqp (CVE-2026-72900, MEDIUM, 2026-08-06) states that a low-privilege user reading the application database via a native query against the audit DB gets 'user session records and bcrypt password hashes', and then adds -- 'On any instance without MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY set (the default), the same read returns the stored credentials for every connected database in cleartext.' That advisory's fix (x.63.5) is already on the pin, so the READ path is closed; this row is about the storage posture that turned that read from a hash dump into a credential dump, and which survives every version bump. SEQUENCING NOTE, because getting this wrong is worse than not doing it: setting the key on an instance that already holds secrets does NOT retro-encrypt them -- Metabase encrypts on write. If the key is introduced after a data source exists, run the one-shot `rotate-encryption-key` command, and once set the key must never be lost or every encrypted row becomes unreadable. Setting it NOW, while metabase_database holds only the sample row, is the cheapest possible moment and needs no rotation step at all. IMPLEMENTATION that matches estate doctrine: add MB_ENCRYPTION_SECRET_KEY to the role compose template sourced from a credentials.yml secret in the {{ global_password_prefix }}_pw_* family (or, once P1 lands, an HKDF-derived scope), NOT a literal in default.config.yml. VERDICT: exploitable only after an operator attaches a real data source; today it is a pre-positioned defect rather than a live exposure, and it is cheapest to fix in exactly that state.

items.current_version: v0.63.5 live; site-url setting = http://127.0.0.1:3002 (read from GET /api/session/properties and from the `setting` table in the app DB)
items.fix_version: config_change: set MB_SITE_URL to https://<metabase_domain> in roles/pazny.metabase/templates/compose.yml.j2 (and, once set, consider redirect-all-requests-to-https).
items.remediation_detail: Cycle-29 batch-52 ATTACK PROBE (tls_crypto_weakness). THE MEASUREMENT: the live instance's `site-url` is `http://127.0.0.1:3002` and `redirect-all-requests-to-https` is false. It got there by self-detection -- nothing in the compose template sets MB_SITE_URL, so Metabase recorded the first URL it was reached on, which was the loopback port-map used by the health probe, not the operator-facing Traefik route. MB_EMBEDDING_APP_ORIGIN is set correctly to https://os.pazny.eu, which is exactly why this was invisible: the template looks like it knows the estate's public origin. WHY A SCHEME STRING IS A CRYPTO FINDING: Metabase derives the `Secure` attribute of its cookies from the site-url SCHEME, not from the scheme of the request it is answering. LIVE-CONFIRMED on the cookie it issues to anonymous callers: `Set-Cookie: metabase.DEVICE=<redacted>; HttpOnly; Path=/; Expires=...2046...; SameSite=Lax` -- HttpOnly and SameSite are present, `Secure` is NOT. CONFIDENCE SPLIT, stated rather than blurred: the missing Secure flag on metabase.DEVICE is MEASURED (high confidence). The same absence on `metabase.SESSION` is INFERRED (medium confidence) -- it is written by the same cookie path and gated by the same site-url scheme per upstream docs, but this scan could not log in to observe it, because the forward_auth posture means the Metabase account is shared and its password was not used here. CONSEQUENCE, scoped to this estate: users reach Metabase at https://metabase.<tld> through Traefik, so the cookie is SET over TLS but is not marked Secure, which means the browser will also send it over plaintext http:// to that same host -- an on-path LAN or Tailscale attacker who can get the browser to emit one http request to the Metabase hostname (an image tag, a redirect, an sslstrip on a sibling page) harvests a live session, and that session is the SHARED query-capable identity described in REM-198. The HSTS header Metabase itself emits (`Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000`) does NOT save this: a browser ignores HSTS delivered over plaintext, and it was observed here on a plaintext response. Whether Traefik re-asserts HSTS on the public route is a separate question this probe did not test. SECOND CONSEQUENCE, non-crypto but same root cause: Metabase builds password-reset and public-share links from site-url, so any reset mail this instance sends contains a link to http://127.0.0.1:3002 -- unusable for a real user, and a plaintext URL carrying a reset token. That endpoint family is the same one GHSA-vwf4-m7j8-wcjf (CVE-2026-72898) told operators to block. VERDICT: exploitable for the session-theft leg given an on-path position (which the LAN listener population of REM-154 shows is not hypothetical here), theoretical for anything requiring reset mail (no mail path is wired to real users on this instance). FIX: set MB_SITE_URL explicitly in the compose template from the same {{ metabase_domain }} expression the Traefik router derives, so the setting cannot drift to whichever URL happens to touch the instance first. This is a one-line render change; the existing app-DB row is overwritten by the env var on next boot.

items.current_version: grafana/tempo:2.10.3 (default.config.yml:1486), live as observability-tempo-1 on networks observability_observability_net + shared_net
items.fix_version: config_change: drop tempo from {{ stacks_shared_network }} in roles/pazny.tempo/templates/compose.yml.j2 (observability_net alone carries the Grafana + Alloy path), or bind the receivers/HTTP API to the observability interface only.
items.remediation_detail:
Cycle-29 batch-52 ATTACK PROBE (tls_crypto_weakness) -- and it lands as a REACHABILITY finding because the crypto question answered itself: Tempo speaks no TLS on any of its three ports, has no auth extension configured, and does not need one IF it is loopback-only. It is not. THE PORT MAPS ARE HONEST AND IRRELEVANT, which is the same lesson REM-194 recorded against Traefik in batch-50 and the reason this probe checked the fabric rather than the host: compose publishes 3200/4327/4328 as `127.0.0.1:

:

`, and `netstat -an` confirms all three are host-loopback. But tempo.yaml.j2 binds the OTLP receivers to `0.0.0.0` inside the container, the HTTP API likewise (`http_listen_address: ""`), and the container joins the flat `shared_net` alongside ~40 peers from every other stack. LIVE-PROVEN FROM A CROSS-STACK PEER, not from the template -- executed inside data-metabase-1 (the `data` stack, a service with no legitimate business talking to Tempo at all): `GET http://tempo:3200/ready` -> 200; `GET http://tempo:3200/status/config` -> the full effective configuration, unauthenticated, in plaintext; `GET http://tempo:3200/api/search?limit=2` -> 200 with a well-formed result body; `POST http://tempo:4328/v1/traces` -> 200, i.e. the ingest path accepts writes from that peer too. WHAT IT BUYS AN ATTACKER, ranked: (a) READ of the whole trace store via the query API -- traces routinely carry request URLs, headers, and internal hostnames, so this is a disclosure primitive proportional to whatever the estate traces, which today is modest and tomorrow is not; (b) WRITE of forged spans -- an attacker who has compromised any container can inject fabricated traces or bury a real one under volume, which corrupts exactly the evidence an incident responder would reach for, and Tempo's only defence is the per-tenant rate limit (burst_size_bytes 20000000) already in the config; (c) config disclosure via /status/config. WHAT IT DOES NOT BUY, measured rather than assumed -- and this is the leg that keeps the severity at MEDIUM: the config leak carries NO secrets on this estate. `storage.trace.backend: local` (path /var/lib/tempo/blocks), and every credential-shaped field in the dump (`access_key`, `secret_key`, `sse`, the sasl/ldap `password` entries -- 16 grep hits) is an empty string from the unused GCS/S3/Kafka sections. That is precisely the exposure CVE-2026-28377 / REM-036 was about (S3 SSE-C key disclosed through /status/config), so it is worth stating plainly: the pin 2.10.3 fixed that bug, AND the local-storage choice means there is no key to disclose either way. Two independent reasons, both currently true. PRECONDITION, stated so this is not read as an internet-facing hole: every vector above requires the attacker to already be executing inside SOME container on shared_net. This is a lateral-movement and evidence-integrity finding, not an entry point. It belongs in the same family as REM-194 (Traefik dashboard reachable across the same fabric) and is more evidence for the standing structural item: `shared_net` is a flat trust domain that services join by default, and membership is not derived from any declared dependency. FIX, cheapest first: Tempo's only legitimate peers are Grafana (datasource) and Alloy (exporter, which reaches it over the HOST loopback at localhost:4327, not over the docker network at all -- see files/anatomy/plugins/alloy-base/templates/config.alloy.j2). Removing `{{ stacks_shared_network }}` from the tempo service should therefore cost nothing; verify Grafana's datasource still resolves `tempo` on observability_net after the change.

items.current_version: n8nio/n8n:2.35.0 live as iiab-n8n-1; roles/pazny.n8n/templates/compose.yml.j2 sets no N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY (repo-wide grep: zero hits)
items.fix_version: config_change: set N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY from a managed secret (credentials.yml / Infisical), matching the value already generated in the volume so existing credentials keep decrypting.
items.remediation_detail: Cycle-29 batch-52 ATTACK PROBE (tls_crypto_weakness). n8n encrypts stored third-party credentials at rest with a symmetric key. The estate does not supply one: a repo-wide grep for N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY returns nothing, and `docker exec iiab-n8n-1 env` confirms it absent at runtime, so n8n did what it does by default -- generated a key on first boot and wrote it to /home/node/.n8n/config. MEASURED CO-LOCATION, which is the whole finding: `ls -la /home/node/.n8n/` shows `config` (0600, 56 bytes) sitting in the SAME directory and the SAME docker volume as `database.sqlite` (1.6 MB), which is where the encrypted credentials live -- this deployment runs n8n on its bundled SQLite, not on the estate Postgres. One `docker exec ... cat /home/node/.n8n/config` returns `{"encryptionKey": "..."}` in plaintext. Encryption at rest whose key ships in the adjacent file protects against exactly one thing: someone who reads the database file and not the directory it is in. OPERATIONAL NOTE, because this scan created the condition: the key value was materialised into this scan's output and is deliberately NOT recorded in this queue. Treat it as disclosed-to-the-scan-transcript and rotate it as part of the fix if the transcript is retained anywhere the credential store is not. Rotation is destructive by design -- changing the key invalidates every stored credential and each must be re-entered -- so it is an operator decision, not an auto-fix. THE OTHER HALF, which matters more than the confidentiality argument: the key is UNMANAGED. It exists only inside a container volume, is not in credentials.yml, not in Infisical, and is not part of any backup-restore contract. Restore the n8n data dir onto a fresh container without that file and every credential in the instance is unrecoverable ciphertext; conversely a `nos --remove=data` regenerates a new key silently, so a later restore of an older volume half-works. This is the availability face of the same defect and it fails quietly, which is the failure mode CLAUDE.md's own 'success markers must be written by a reader' rule was written about. WHAT IS ALREADY RIGHT, so the fix does not get over-scoped: N8N_PROTOCOL is https, so n8n marks its session cookie Secure (contrast REM-200, where Metabase does not) -- this component's transport posture is sound and the finding is purely about key custody. The SMTP relay runs N8N_SMTP_SSL=false, but it points at Mailpit over the docker network for dev mail capture, with no credentials and no external hop: mitigated, recorded so a future probe does not re-derive it. VERDICT: not exploitable on its own -- reading the key requires exec into the container or read access to the volume, which is post-compromise or host-level. It is a defence-in-depth defect that makes any container-escape or backup-disclosure event strictly worse, plus a live restore-integrity gap. FIX: read the existing key out of the volume once, store it as a managed secret, and render it as N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY in the compose template. Supplying the SAME value is a no-op for existing credentials and closes the custody gap without a rotation.

items.current_version: nos-bone (host launchd eu.thisisait.nos.bone) live as ~/bone/venv uvicorn main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8099; no mem_limit (host process); files/anatomy/bone/main.py declares no body-size middleware and no --limit-* uvicorn flags in roles/pazny.bone/templates/bone.plist.j2
items.fix_version: config_change: reject oversized bodies BEFORE parsing -- add an ASGI/Starlette Content-Length + streamed-size guard (a small middleware that 413s when Content-Length or accumulated stream bytes exceed a cap, e.g. 1-4 MB for the JSON control-plane endpoints), so the HMAC/scope gate is reached without first buffering the whole body. The /vfs/upload path already models the correct pattern (streamed, capped at _MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES).
items.remediation_detail: Cycle-30 batch-53 ATTACK PROBE (resource_exhaustion_vectors), Bone. FastAPI endpoints that declare a `body: dict` / `body: dict | None` parameter cause Starlette to read the ENTIRE request body (request.body() concatenates every request.stream() chunk into one in-memory bytes object) and JSON-parse it into a Python dict BEFORE the function body runs. On the two HMAC-authenticated ingestion endpoints -- POST /api/events + /api/v1/events (events_ingest) and POST /api/v1/notifications (notifications_ingest) -- the HMAC verification is performed INSIDE the function body (verify_hmac(x_wing_timestamp, x_wing_signature, raw)), i.e. strictly AFTER the full body has already been buffered and parsed. There is no Content-Length guard, no body-size middleware (grep of main.py for add_middleware/Middleware/max.*body returns nothing), and no uvicorn --limit-* flag in the plist. Bone is a HOST launchd process with NO memory limit (contrast every Docker service, which carries mem_limit). LIVE-CONFIRMED 2026-08-15: a single unauthenticated `curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8099/api/v1/events --data-binary @20MB.json` with NO HMAC headers returned `HTTP 401 {"detail":"HMAC check failed: missing HMAC headers"}` with size_upload=20971544 -- proving the 20 MB body was accepted and buffered in full before the 401 was emitted. Because the buffer is unbounded and the process is unlimited, a caller can drive bone's RSS to an arbitrary multiple of the request size (deeply-nested JSON also amplifies CPU during parse); scaling to multi-GB was deliberately NOT executed against the live estate to avoid OOM-ing the operator's host, but the mechanism (full buffer strictly before auth) is proven and scaling is arithmetic. REACHABILITY: bone binds 127.0.0.1:8099 and is EXCLUDED from Traefik (traefik_auth_modes.bone='none', listed under the Traefik exclusion set 'Bone is on host; published only on 127.0.0.1; reach via Wing UI'), so this is NOT internet- or LAN-facing. It is reachable by (a) any local host process and (b) any Docker container in the estate via host.docker.internal:8099 (Docker Desktop for Mac maps host.docker.internal to the host loopback -- the same container->loopback trust surface SEC-6 hardened for Wing's :9000 bind). VERDICT: exploitable as a PRE-AUTH local/container-scoped denial-of-service against the audit+telemetry backbone; not remotely reachable and not a confidentiality/integrity breach. Rated MEDIUM: the buffer-before-auth defect is real and unauthenticated, but the loopback-only reachability makes it a post-foothold or malicious-local-process amplifier rather than an edge-exposed vector. The same `body: dict` pattern is used on ~14 other POST endpoints (scope/JWT-guarded via Depends); FastAPI may resolve those Depends before body parse, so this row is deliberately scoped to the two endpoints where auth is provably downstream of the parse and where a live 401-after-full-upload was observed.
items.source: live: curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8099/api/v1/events (20MB unauth body -> HTTP 401 size_upload=20971544, 2026-08-15) ; files/anatomy/bone/main.py:691-740 (events_ingest), 782+ (notifications_ingest) ; files/anatomy/bone/vfs.py:267-294 (the correct streamed+capped counter-pattern, _MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES=128MiB) ; roles/pazny.bone/templates/bone.plist.j2 (no --limit flags) ; roles/pazny.traefik/vars/main.yml:39,195 (bone=none, Traefik-excluded)

items.remediation_detail: Cycle-31 batch-54 CVE scan (2026-08-16, supply_chain_freshness). The pin is TWO security releases behind: default.config.yml:1326 reads wordpress_version 7.0.2 and live iiab-wordpress-1 runs wordpress:7.0.2 (digest sha256:b2d7e3153c8a96f90305a3102fb6439335237fb1a9655b617d15c5168ce2f7a3, up 6 days, healthy). (1) WordPress 7.0.3 (2026-08-06) fixes TWELVE issues. The headline is CVE-2026-64638 (CVSS 8.9 HIGH, reported by pwn.ai): a PRE-AUTHENTICATION reflected XSS on the login screen that can escalate to PHP code execution. Patchstack's write-up is the honest ceiling here -- the RCE leg is not drive-by; it requires phishing an Administrator into clicking the crafted link, so the unauth reach is the XSS and the RCE is the post-click consequence. The other eleven: stored XSS in emoji settings / Post Content block / Quick Edit / Post Date block (all Contributor+), multisite privilege escalation (multisite WITH open registration only -- N/A here), information disclosure via the Latest Comments block, post-slug enumeration, comment-feed disclosure, a CSS-injection bypass (Author+), an email-confirmation bypass, and an SSRF. Several reach back to WordPress 4.7. (2) WordPress 7.0.4 (2026-08-12) fixes an AUTHENTICATED Author+ remote code execution via malicious file upload 'on sites that use Imagick and Ghostscript' (pwn.ai). The revised file is exactly one: /wp-includes/class-wp-image-editor-imagick.php. LIVE-VERIFIED that this estate satisfies the 7.0.4 precondition, which is the reason this row is HIGH rather than MEDIUM: `docker exec iiab-wordpress-1 php -m` lists imagick, `which gs` returns /usr/bin/gs at Ghostscript 10.05.1, and the ACTIVE policy set in /etc/ImageMagick-7/policy.xml (comments stripped before reading -- the stock file's example stanzas are commented out and a naive grep reads as a deny-all) denies only the URL/HTTPS/HTTP coders plus path '@*'. The PS / EPS / PDF coders and the Ghostscript delegate are NOT denied, so the Imagick->gs path an Author+ upload needs is open. ACTION: bump wordpress_version 7.0.2 -> 7.0.4 in default.config.yml:1326 (grep-confirmed the role default does not shadow it). Target tag verified present: registry-1.docker.io library/wordpress:7.0.4 -> HTTP 200, pushed 2026-08-13T03:15Z across all php8.2-8.5 apache/fpm/alpine variants. Do NOT stop at 7.0.3 (it exists -- 20 tags pushed 2026-08-11/12, contrary to a first read of the truncated Hub tag page -- but it is itself superseded and still carries the Imagick/Ghostscript RCE). PARTIAL MITIGATION meanwhile: install_wordpress defaults false; Authentik native_oidc fronts the site, so 'Author+' means an Authentik principal holding a WordPress Author role, not an anonymous signup. That does nothing for the CVE-2026-64638 pre-auth XSS, which is reachable by anyone who can load wp-login.php. NOTE this row compounds REM-163 (still open, re-verified unfixed this batch): the auth cookie is issued without the Secure attribute, so an XSS/network position on the login path is worth more here than on a correctly-configured install.

items.fix_version: n/a -- bump-target hazard; the correct 18.11 terminal is 18.11.9-ce.0, never 18.11.8-ce.0
items.remediation_detail: Cycle-31 batch-54 ATTACK PROBE (supply_chain_freshness), GitLab. A withdrawn release is still being served as a container tag, and the withdrawal notice exists only in vendor PROSE -- nothing in the registry marks it. GitLab shipped 18.11.8 on 2026-08-05, then discovered that deprecation code in it 'enabled Mattermost incorrectly', which breaks upgrades to 19.x on Linux package installs even when Mattermost was never configured. GitLab PULLED the 18.11.8 omnibus package and replaced it with 18.11.9 (2026-08-06), and the release notes tell operators to clear local 18.11.8 caches. But the CONTAINER tag was not withdrawn alongside the package: registry-1.docker.io gitlab/gitlab-ce:18.11.8-ce.0 -> HTTP 200, pushed 2026-08-05T12:49:42Z, still anonymously pullable today (18.11.9-ce.0 pushed 2026-08-06T09:34:40Z, also 200). WHY THIS IS A ROW AND NOT A CURIOSITY: nOS resolves bump targets by reading registry tag lists, and the estate's own upgrade-advisor agent authors recipes the same way. Anything that picks 'the highest 18.11.x tag' lands on 18.11.8 -- the known-bad build -- and the registry gives it no signal to the contrary. This is the version-pin analogue of the lesson already recorded for REM-178: a recorded target below (or beside) what the vendor actually blesses re-opens the gap for whoever acts on it. Two caveats kept explicit rather than smoothed over: (a) the withdrawal GitLab describes is of the Linux PACKAGE, and the Docker image -- though built from omnibus -- is distributed separately, so whether the 18.11.8 CONTAINER carries the same Mattermost defect is NOT verified here; (b) nOS is unaffected today because it pins 18.11.7-ce.0 explicitly and never resolves a floating tag. ACTION: none to the running estate. This is a guard-rail item -- when REM-159's bump is executed, the 18.11 line's terminal build is 18.11.9-ce.0 and 18.11.8-ce.0 must be excluded by name. Worth encoding in upgrades/gitlab.yml as an explicit skip so a future automated bump cannot select it.

items.fix_version: n/a -- retire roles/pazny.freepbx or repoint at a maintained image
items.remediation_detail: Cycle-31 batch-54 ATTACK PROBE (supply_chain_freshness), FreePBX. The image this role pins is no longer published. roles/pazny.freepbx/templates/compose.yml.j2:12 renders tiredofit/freepbx:{{ freepbx_version }} with freepbx_version 'latest' (default.config.yml:2249), and that reference no longer resolves anonymously: hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/tiredofit/freepbx/ -> HTTP 404, and an anonymous Docker Hub pull-scope token against registry-1.docker.io/v2/tiredofit/freepbx/tags/list -> HTTP 401 UNAUTHORIZED. CONTROLS RUN so this is not read off a broken probe: grafana/grafana -> hub 200 / registry 200; linuxserver/bookstack -> hub 200; and critically tiredofit/freescout -> hub 200, which shows the tiredofit NAMESPACE is alive and publishing -- it is this one REPOSITORY that is gone. (A `docker pull` cross-check could not be completed: the host's Docker credential helper hangs and the CLI aborts with 'error getting credentials'; the registry-API evidence above stands on its own.) TWO CONSEQUENCES. (1) AVAILABILITY, today: install_freepbx=true on a fresh host now HARD-FAILS at image pull rather than deploying a vulnerable PBX. The voip stack would bring up zero containers and trip the guard at tasks/stacks/stack-up.yml:498 ('FAIL only if any stack has zero running containers -- image pull / compose abort'). An operator enabling FreePBX gets a failed converge, not a warning. The live estate is untouched: install_freepbx is false, no freepbx container is in `docker ps` (62 running), and no tiredofit/freepbx layer is in the local image cache. (2) LATENT SUPPLY-CHAIN, theoretical: a deleted Docker Hub repository name is a dangling reference. Combined with a fully floating ':latest' tag, zero digest pinning (see REM-207) and no content trust, anything that made that name re-registrable would be pulled and run as trusted. Rated THEORETICAL, not exploitable: the namespace remains under the original owner's control, so re-registration presupposes an account compromise. STRUCTURAL DISPOSITION: this closes the question the four vendor-blocked FreePBX rows left hanging. REM-014 (CVE-2025-57819, CVSS 10.0), REM-046, REM-113 (CVE-2026-46376) and REM-130 (GHSA-37j8-fhxx-9vhp) are all blocked on 'no path to a fix in this image, image abandoned 2022-04-30'. The image is now not merely abandoned but ABSENT, so freepbx is undeployable rather than deployable-and-unpatched. The role should be retired or repointed at a maintained image; leaving a dead pin in the tree is a trap for the next operator who flips the flag. Those four rows stay vendor-blocked -- their disposition is unchanged and this row does not close them.

items.remediation_detail: Cycle-31 batch-54 ATTACK PROBE (supply_chain_freshness), estate-wide. Three measurements that are individually defensible and jointly mean the estate has no content-integrity anchor for any image it runs. (1) NO DIGEST PINNING: `grep -E '^\s*image:' roles/*/templates/compose.yml.j2` matches 52 role compose templates; the count carrying an '@sha256:' digest is ZERO. Every service is pulled by tag. For immutable-by-convention version tags (wordpress:7.0.2, gitlab/gitlab-ce:18.11.7-ce.0) that is conventional and low-risk; for a genuinely floating tag it is not, and at least one role ships freepbx_version 'latest' (see REM-206). (2) NO RE-PULL ON CONVERGE: main.yml:473 sets _docker_compose_pull to '--pull always' only when version_policy is 'latest' or 'lts'. default.config.yml:348 sets version_policy 'stable', so the flag renders EMPTY at every one of its five consumers (core-up.yml:442,504; stack-up.yml:199,271; apps-up.yml:78) and `docker compose up -d` re-pulls nothing once an image is cached locally. A tag whose CONTENT is republished at the registry -- the normal case for ':latest', and the abnormal-but-real case for a retagged version -- is never re-fetched. The estate silently freezes on whatever was pulled first. (3) NO RECORD OF WHAT IS DEPLOYED: docs/llm/security/versions.json contains the string 'sha256' zero times. It records intended TAGS, not deployed CONTENT. Digests exist and are readable -- `docker image inspect --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}'` returns them for all four live components in this batch (recorded in REM-204 and in the scan-state notes) -- they are simply never captured. WHY IT MATTERS HERE RATHER THAN IN THE ABSTRACT: (1)+(3) together mean that if a tag's content were swapped upstream, nOS could neither prevent the swap nor DETECT it after the fact, because nothing on disk says what content was ever trusted. (2) means the reverse failure is equally silent -- an operator who believes ':latest' tracks upstream is running a frozen image with no signal. This is the same shape as the standing doctrine that a success marker must be written by a reader, not by the attempting code: the queue records the version we INTENDED to deploy and calls it the version deployed. ACTION (graduated, none urgent): (a) capture RepoDigests into versions.json during the existing scan so drift becomes observable -- this is the cheap half and needs no converge; (b) digest-pin the roles whose tag is genuinely floating rather than all 52, so the pin discipline stays reviewable; (c) decide deliberately whether 'stable' should imply --pull, given that today it silently means 'never refresh'. Rated MEDIUM: no exploitation path is demonstrated, and no tag swap is alleged or observed. This is a missing detection and integrity control, not an active exposure.
items.source: in-repo measurement: roles/*/templates/compose.yml.j2 (52 image: refs, 0 @sha256) ; main.yml:473 ; default.config.yml:348 ; docs/llm/security/versions.json ; docker image inspect RepoDigests on the 4 live batch components

items.remediation_detail: Cycle-33 batch-55 SCAN (2026-08-19, version_header_leakage), successor to REM-165. UPSTREAM SEVERITY IS CRITICAL CVSS 9.9 -- filed HIGH on nOS context alone, and the gap between those two numbers is the whole content of this row. GHSA-6w83-8777-v93q, published 2026-08-13, NO CVE ASSIGNED: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H, CWE-1336. Server-side template injection through user-controlled message fields lets an authenticated user holding an ORDINARY OPERATIONAL role evaluate template expressions with an unrestricted context -- arbitrary database operations, document deletion, outbound requests and mail sent from the server. Vendor states no workaround exists; patching is the only remedy. Affects erpnext < 15.119.1 and < 16.32.0; fixed 15.119.1 / 16.32.0. THE PIN IS INSIDE THE WINDOW BY ONE PATCH: default.config.yml:2220 reads v15.119.0 and the floor is 15.119.1. THIS IS THE THIRD CONSECUTIVE TIME AN ERPNEXT PIN HAS BEEN OVERTAKEN BETWEEN SCANS, and the interval is now the story -- v15.119.0 was chosen on 2026-08-05 for REM-165 and was already obsolete eight days later. Method, stated so it is repeatable rather than re-derived: the verdict was NOT reached by reading the advisory list. All 62 repo advisories were fetched from api.github.com/repos/frappe/erpnext/security-advisories and every v15 fixed-version was compared against the pin as a version tuple; that filter returns exactly one row, this one. Eyeballing would have failed -- the 2026-08-13/14 wave alone is 40+ advisories and FOUR of them fix at exactly 15.119.0 (GHSA-8pr6-r75h-h8xx, GHSA-q8wq-q35q-gj8h, GHSA-m5xh-ghvj-xjrv, GHSA-48wc-j2qh-rcgw), i.e. cleared by the pin with zero margin and trivially mis-read as affected. THIRTY-ONE of that wave carry NO CVE ID, including this one, so a CVE-keyed feed sees none of it -- the same blind spot recorded for batch-43 and batch-39, now measured at scale. FRAPPE FRAMEWORK ships in the same image and is NOT cleared by this bump alone: frappe advisories reach v15 floors of 15.115.0 (CVE-2026-66003 HIGH, access-control bypass via REST API, published 2026-08-18 -- one day before this scan) and 15.114.0 (CVE-2026-66001 HIGH, improper authorization in the OAuth2 consent endpoint); three more (CVE-2026-53569, CVE-2026-62315, CVE-2026-63654) publish with vulnerable_version_range 'tbd' and CANNOT be version-keyed at all -- flagged, not scored. The bundled frappe version for a given erpnext tag was not measured here (nothing is deployed to measure), so frappe coverage is MEDIUM confidence. ZERO LIVE EXPOSURE, re-verified this batch and not inherited: install_erpnext resolves FALSE via tools/estate-status.py --config (default.config.yml:471, no config.yml override), the role is hard-blocked at load behind erpnext_experimental_override, it is excluded from profiles/all-on.yml, and `docker ps` shows no erpnext container. The SSTI needs an authenticated session against a server that does not exist. ACTION: this is the UPDATED acceptance criterion for the deferred ERPNext rework (REM-008) -- do not enable erpnext below v15.119.1; set default.config.yml:2220 to v15.119.3 (published 2026-08-18, confirmed present upstream) so the criterion carries margin instead of landing on the floor for the fourth time. Kept PENDING so the moving target stays visible. REM-017/041/115/133/165 remain resolved at the pin.

items.remediation_detail: Cycle-33 batch-55 ATTACK PROBE (version_header_leakage), and the finding of record for this probe class across the five-component batch. ONLYOFFICE is the ONLY component of the five that discloses its build to an ANONYMOUS caller AT THE EDGE, measured through Traefik on 443 with a Host header and no credential -- not inferred from the compose template, and not merely on the loopback bind. TWO ENDPOINTS, both HTTP/2 200: (1) GET https://office.<tld>/index.html returns 'Server is functioning normally. Version: 9.3.1. Build: 37.'; (2) GET https://office.<tld>/web-apps/apps/api/documents/api.js returns a banner comment 'Version: 9.3.1 (build:59)'. No Server: header version is leaked -- the header reads a bare 'server: nginx' -- so a header-only probe would have reported this component CLEAN. The disclosure is in the BODY, which is why this row exists. WHY IT IS REACHABLE AND WHY THAT IS NOT A MISCONFIGURATION: traefik_auth_modes.onlyoffice = 'none' BY DESIGN (roles/pazny.traefik/vars/main.yml:42) -- collaborative editing cannot sit behind forward-auth because the Nextcloud/Outline/BookStack integrations call it server-to-server -- so there is no gate to add here without breaking the service. The JWT gate (JWT_ENABLED=true) protects the document and conversion API and is unaffected; static assets are served ahead of it. WHAT THE DISCLOSURE IS WORTH, stated honestly: it is RECON, not access. Rated LOW because no ONLYOFFICE/DocumentServer advisory is outstanding against this build -- the vendor's repo advisory endpoint returns ZERO published advisories, permanently, for the third consecutive scan. Its real cost is that it hands an attacker the exact build to match against a future disclosure, on a service with no auth wall in front of it, and it does so for a build that is NOT the declared pin. THE PROBE INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATES REM-170 FROM THE OUTSIDE: that row established by in-container dpkg that the running build is euro-office-documentserver 9.3.1-dev.1 while the declared pin is 9.3.1.2; this probe reaches the same conclusion anonymously from the network, with the served string '9.3.1' matching the dev build and not the pin. Both re-verified this batch: dpkg still reports 9.3.1-dev.1, and the resident image digest is unchanged at sha256:5a1a8b7083856b309f09a5b06aa96f80182cbdfccddcae6c082ecf7a2b3cbf2b (created 2026-06-25T09:38:48Z) -- the floating 'latest' tag has not moved in the 14 days since REM-170, which is luck, not control. ACTION, in order of value: (a) close REM-170 first -- pinning the image by digest is what makes the disclosed version MEAN something; suppressing the string while the tag still floats hides drift rather than fixing it; (b) optionally suppress the banner at the edge, but note the honest ceiling: index.html can be handled with a Traefik/nginx response rewrite, whereas api.js is a JavaScript asset the integrations fetch and its comment header cannot be stripped without a sub_filter on a cached/compressed body -- more fragility than a LOW recon leak justifies. RECOMMENDATION: accept (b) as residual and documented, fix (a). MEASURED-CLEAN COMPARATORS from the same probe, recorded so the negative result is not re-derived: homeassistant returns a deliberately BLANKED 'Server:' header (empty string) on every path and leaks no version; firefly returns a bare 'server: nginx' and 302s anonymous callers to Authentik; ntfy leaks no version string at all.
items.source: live probe 2026-08-19 via Traefik 443 (--resolve, anonymous, no credential); docker exec dpkg -l; docker image inspect

summary.note: SUMMARY TALLY RECOMPUTED FROM THE ROWS 2026-08-19 (cycle-33 batch-55: erpnext, homeassistant, firefly, onlyoffice, ntfy; attack-probe focus version_header_leakage). TWO rows added, ONE pending row CLOSED by reconciliation, and it required no new work: REM-165 (erpnext) was already satisfied on the live estate -- the pin had advanced to the exact v15.119.0 the row asked for, and the role-default shadow it named no longer exists. That is the twelve-rows-already-live pattern again; CLAUDE.md's warning that a pending row is not proof of exposure earned its place. REM-168 (homeassistant) was ALREADY resolved on 2026-08-10 with no evidence recorded, so it was not closed by this batch -- it was independently RE-VERIFIED live and given the detail it lacked: login_attempts_threshold: 10 and ip_ban_enabled: true are rendered IN THE RUNNING CONTAINER, which is the only evidence that can close a row whose whole finding was that an enabled-looking ban banned nothing. REM-208 (erpnext HIGH, upstream CRITICAL 9.9) is the batch headline: GHSA-6w83-8777-v93q, no CVE, SSTI to unrestricted-context execution, fixes at 15.119.1 -- the pin misses by ONE PATCH, eight days after being set. It was found by comparing all 62 repo advisories against the pin as version tuples; eyeballing would have failed, because four separate advisories in the 2026-08-13/14 wave fix at exactly 15.119.0 and 31 of that wave carry no CVE id at all. REM-209 (onlyoffice LOW) is the probe's finding of record: onlyoffice is the only one of the five that discloses its build anonymously at the edge, and it does so in the response BODY while its Server header reads a bare 'nginx' -- a header-only probe would have called it clean. The disclosed '9.3.1' corroborates REM-170's dev-build finding from outside the host. THE METHODOLOGICAL RESULT OF THIS BATCH IS AN INVERSION OF THE LAST ONE, and it belongs in the tally because acting on either half alone leaves a hole: batch-43 concluded 'query the vendor repo endpoint or see nothing' after OSV missed a critical ERPNext RCE. That holds -- but for Home Assistant it fails in the opposite direction. CVE-2026-64824 (Core < 2026.7.0, symlink path-traversal to root RCE via backup-restore) is ABSENT from all 23 home-assistant/core repo advisories and present in the CVE feed and OSV. Batch-43 queried the repo endpoint, declared the CVE leg clean, and was wrong: the estate ran the affected 2026.6.0 for the fifteen days between that CVE publishing and the 2026-08-11 sweep to 2026.8.1, which closed it as currency work with no idea it was closing an RCE. Neither source is sufficient; both must be queried. One data-quality trap recorded so it is not propagated: OSV lists GHSA-78r8-wwqv-r299 as an alias of CVE-2026-64824, but that GHSA is a PraisonAI advisory -- do NOT cite it for Home Assistant. Also corrected rather than appended to: REM-167's stated Authentik mitigation is FALSIFIED -- ntfy's forward-auth was deliberately removed 2026-08-08 so phones could subscribe -- while its severity survives, because publish rights now require a credential in ntfy's own user DB. Its second leg, the v2.27.0 config-hash secret leak, was traced through the actual server/config.go diff and found NOT APPLICABLE: every field the fix excludes is empty in nOS, so no row was filed for it. REM-166 (firefly) and REM-170 (onlyoffice) re-confirmed unfixed with targets verified present upstream; REM-166's target moves 6.6.3 -> 6.6.6 to avoid landing in GHSA-5q8v's 6.4.23-6.5.0 window. FOUR of these five components are LIVE despite every prior batch citing install_X=false as a mitigation -- config.yml flips ntfy, homeassistant, firefly and onlyoffice to true, and only erpnext is genuinely absent.
